item.description: El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días. Zelenski señaló que Ucrania está dispuesta a participar en conversaciones de paz durante la cumbre del G20 en Estados Unidos, pero que, hasta el momento, no se había recibido ninguna invitación al respecto. "Hay claramente una cuestión en juego: obligar a Rusia a poner fin a esta guerra", dijo el mandatario a periodistas en Kiev. "Es posible (...) con la mediación del presidente (Donald) Trump y de nuestros socios. Creo que todo es posible, y podemos contar con una reunión en Florida durante la cumbre del G20", agregó.

item.title: Why Anthropic is turning away some users
item.description: Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy. Over 30 years, he’s developed a methodology for spotting business ideas and used it to help start 175 companies through his incubator, with more than 45 exits. So it stung a little when, a few months ago, Gross found that AI had gotten disturbingly good at generating business ideas. He told me it left him feeling “depressed”. Then the feeling turned into an idea itself: what if he turned his methodology into a system anyone could use? That system, Idealab.ai , launched this week. It matches your background and skills against AI-generated business ideas, and lets you set the budget you’re willing to work with. Not every idea it spits out is going to be a great business, but Gross is betting the platform can lower the barrier to entrepreneurship for people who’d never otherwise know where to start. The human part, he insists, doesn’t go away. “All the judgment and decisions still have to be made by humans,” he told me. AI can offer suggestions, “but you have to make the call.” And, “you’ve got to be passionate about it, for sure.” OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger is 'a good idea' as companies form deal committees"] [USN:FWN4661WE TEXT:"Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centers popular"] [USN:L6N46701V TEXT:"OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system"] [USN:L4N4660IQ TEXT:"Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows"] [USN:L6N4661EP TEXT:"SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production, Musk says"] [USN:L8N4650GT TEXT:"ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders"] ANTHROPIC'S FIGHT WITH DISTILLATION Here’s a strange move for a company racing toward the largest IPO in history: turn away paying customers, on purpose, weeks before you go public. That’s effectively what Anthropic just did. Inside an investor meeting in San Francisco last week, my colleagues and I got a [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"behind-the-scenes look"] at how Anthropic’s executives are explaining a slowdown of their own making. The company has cut off a meaningful slice of paying customers — accounting for between 5% and 7% of its revenue in the first nine months of the year, investors at the meeting told us. The reasoning: those accounts weren’t typical customers. They were, Anthropic alleged, Chinese AI labs quietly mining Claude to train their own models. The technique is known as distillation in AI model development. A smaller “student” model learns by studying the outputs of a larger “teacher” model, essentially absorbing its capabilities secondhand. In February, [USN:L4N3ZJ1G1 TEXT:"Anthropic said"] Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax had generated more than 16 million interactions with Claude through roughly 24,000 fake accounts, all in violation of its terms of service. Anthropic calls this more than a contract violation. It considers the practice a loss of intellectual property with national security implications. So the company rolled out new defenses earlier this month: applying access restrictions, proxy blocking, and bans on tens of thousands of accounts, which it says has cut off 90% to 99% of the data being siphoned. Anthropic is telling investors the crackdown has effectively stopped Chinese developers from distilling its models. Here’s why that matters for the IPO: it gives Anthropic a tidy explanation for something investors were already nervous about — a month-to-month growth deceleration. It may also address a bigger worry. Anthropic is betting that cutting off Chinese labs will slow their progress, not just stop a few bad actors from gaming the terms of service. The underlying numbers are still extraordinary by any standard. By this past March, Anthropic had already brought in $4.7 billion in a single quarter — more than all of 2025. Then it kept climbing: $11.6 billion in the second quarter, $16.8 billion in the third. But growth at that scale doesn’t usually keep compounding at the same rate forever. Competition from cheaper, open-source Chinese models remains one of the most common concerns investors are raising. Reuters has reported that [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"some investors are now discussing"] a valuation near $1.5 trillion for the IPO, down from the roughly $2 trillion once expected. The real question is whether this crackdown — and the short-term revenue hit that comes with it — actually buys Anthropic a lasting distance from its open-source rivals, or just a temporary edge. CHART OF THE WEEK According to [USN:L6N4650MN TEXT:"a new survey"] of more than 380 security and technology professionals by Salt Security, 86% of their organizations now have at least one AI agent operating, and 77% have agents chaining actions together across other agents. In other words, agents aren’t just answering questions anymore — they’re taking multi-step actions, often autonomously, deep inside company systems. What’s missing is the ability to actually watch them. Only 18% of those same organizations say they can automatically stop an agent that starts behaving unexpectedly, and just 13% can trace a complete path from instruction to outcome across every agent involved. That’s a massive visibility gap between how fast companies are deploying agents and how well they can monitor what those agents are actually doing.

item.title: The midterms reach Kyiv
item.description: US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, once Washington's most celebrated wartime ally, is finding himself caught in the crossfire of US midterm politics. He is under mounting pressure from Trump to strike a peace deal with Putin. With US voters increasingly frustrated by[USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:" high energy prices"] and the cost of living, Trump has turned renewed attention to the war in Ukraine in recent days, arguing that a negotiated settlement there could help ease economic pressures at home, even though US consumers would be unlikely to feel the effects of any peace deal ahead of the November 3 vote. Trump has said the war may be closer than ever to finishing and that he wants the death and destruction to end. But he also may be betting that a resolution of the four-year conflict could ease pressures on the US economy, voters’ pocketbooks and his own political fortunes. Russia is a major oil supplier and has held out the possibility of a broad economic pact with Washington. In recent weeks, Trump has cut a deal with Putin, temporarily easing US sanctions on Russian diesel (and [USN:FWN4622VQ TEXT:"waiving others"]) in exchange for Moscow providing more diesel to global markets. He’s considering a [USN:SPN45Y0Z6 TEXT:"meeting with Putin"] and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month, without Zelenskiy. Meanwhile, Kyiv has [USN:P8N41Y023 TEXT:"complained that a satellite system"] made by US-based SpaceX has stopped working when mounted on fast-moving drones, limiting its ability to strike Russian targets and defend against attacks. The moves are a shift from Trump’s earlier [USN:S0N3S902L TEXT:"criticisms of Putin"] and a return to [USN:L2N3PI1I7 TEXT:"more prickly relations"] between the US and Ukrainian leaders. Ukraine and several European allies have expressed alarm at an apparent pivot by Trump. Trump has blamed [USN:L8N4620HY TEXT:"Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries"] for driving up global diesel prices. He’s also suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine,” he told us at the White House on Monday. “Zelenskiy is not helping matters much.” Trump envoy Steve Witkoff later called Putin a “humanitarian” for [USN:L8N4670ON TEXT:"freeing a retired US schoolteacher"] in custody since 2022. The Ukrainian attacks have contributed to higher diesel prices, although market analysts attribute most of the increase to disruptions in fuel shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. That’s a consequence of a different war: the US-led one with Iran. Trump wouldn’t be the first politician to lay blame for inflation abroad. His Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, [USN:L2N2VC04A TEXT:"pointed to Putin"] after Russia's invasion of Ukraine caused gasoline prices to surge ahead of congressional elections in 2022. Voters are not buying a similar argument from Trump. Some 78% of Americans say his policies bear at least some blame for rising prices, according to a [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. Most Republicans and Democrats cited the cost of living as their top concern. Zelenskiy told visiting US lawmakers on Monday that recent “decisions on the American side … are [USN:L4N4651HF TEXT:"hard to explain"].” For the answer, he may need to look no further than the US political calendar. TOP US POLITICS HEADLINES Special Report: Nine ways the Trump administration could interfere with the midterms Graphics: What redistricting means for Tennessee voters Podcast: Prediction markets and social good: An interview with Kalshi's CEO [USN:L4N4621CK TEXT:"As Trump's support slips, white evangelicals remain his Republican bedrock"] [USN:L1N4660O3 TEXT:"US Supreme Court rulings reshape midterm election battlefield"] [USN:L6N46108U TEXT:"High gas prices strain Detroit's hungry and food banks ahead of midterm elections"] POLL OF THE WEEK Your questions on election officials’ preparations for violent or legal threats How are election officials preparing for threats to poll workers, misinformation, administrative disruptions or attempts to interfere with voting and vote counting? Reuters interviewed more than 50 state and local election officials from both political parties, including a dozen secretaries of state, the top election officials in their states. Nearly all said they are adopting new strategies to prepare for political interference, misinformation, cyberattacks and even threats of violence ahead of the midterms. Their efforts span jurisdictions large and small, in areas controlled by Trump’s Republican Party as well as the opposition Democratic Party. In Michigan, for example, state officials are advising local clerks on the appropriate response if the federal government demands access to voting machines. Preparations fall into three categories. Some election officials are hiring lawyers or seeking legal skills, as over a dozen interviewees said. Twice that many election officials said they are expanding public outreach and social media campaigns to counter misinformation around the reliability of mail-in voting or voting machines. Most of the interviewed officials said they are scrambling to fill gaps left by the Trump administration’s cuts to programs that help safeguard elections from cyberattacks and physical security threats. That includes ongoing work to fortify election offices with camera systems and bulletproof glass – a trend that began after Trump disputed his loss to Biden in the 2020 election, prompting violent threats by Trump supporters against election workers . Read our reporting on more specific examples of what election officials are doing in preparation for such potential scenarios in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Georgia, Michigan, Colorado, and Maine. THE VIEW FROM PARIS The French government is bracing for the prospect of more protests as soon as this weekend after some of the [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"worst urban tumult"] in years. Thousands were arrested, and shops looted, amid nationwide protests on October 17 over high prices and declining public services. Trump has weighed in repeatedly on the crisis, blaming immigrants and radical Islam for the violence, without providing evidence. In Kansas on Monday, Trump warned voters that the US would [USN:L1N4650ZT TEXT:"burn like France"] if Democrats win. Macron [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"shot back"] that Trump and other foreign leaders had spread misinformation about what happened and were looking to score political points at France's expense. He called comments by foreign leaders "stupid" and "unacceptable." item.title: US blocks two devices with Chinese-made surveillance chips
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules. The US telecom agency said it barred a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter containing chips produced by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which the agency said advertises its chip as "designed for the surveillance market" and including "detection algorithms for human faces." FCC Chair Brendan Carr said video devices containing surveillance chips produced by companies on its national security list "pose an obvious and unacceptable risk to the nation and our people." Huawei did not immediately respond to a request for comment and HiSilicon could not immediately be reached. The FCC voted in July to bar sales of devices in the US that contain key hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks The Trump administration has mounted a sweeping crackdown on Chinese technology gear

item.title: Romania to speed up development of Black Sea capabilities after cargo ship attacks
item.description: Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday. At least [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"seven cargo ships"] have been hit near the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria in the past two weeks, with some 30 sailors reported dead or missing. Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots [USN:L1N46306E TEXT:"shot down"] two of the latest generation of Russian drones over Romanian territorial waters on Saturday. [USN:L6N46613E TEXT:"NATO"] said on Tuesday it will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems and drones to the Black Sea. Romania's top defence council said latest ship attacks are direct consequences of Russia's aggression beyond Ukraine's borders. Threats to freedom of navigation and critical energy projects in the Black Sea pose a security crisis for Romania. The current risks require concrete measures to protect human lives, maintain free access to national ports, and ensure the security of energy facilities in the Exclusive Economic Zone. The top defence council said it will accelerate the development of capabilities for maritime surveillance, countering naval mines and intervening against drones illegally breaching national airspace and waters. Authorities will practice to improve the efficiency of their operational response. Romania will seek to improve cooperation with fellow NATO members [USN:L8N43A0JZ TEXT:"Bulgaria and Turkey"] with whom it shares the Black Sea. "The Council members also analyzed ways to intensify coordination within NATO. This includes strengthening the deterrence and defense posture on the Eastern Flank and identifying new measures to respond to threats in the Black Sea region."

item.title: Nigeria says Ebola case remains isolated, urges calm
item.description: Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently confirmed Ebola case had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection.
item.dc:creator: Camillus Eboh
item.content:encoded: Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently [USN:L6N4670RQ TEXT:"confirmed Ebola case"] had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection. Nigeria reported its first Ebola case in more than a decade on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that health officials have described as the [USN:L6N4421DF TEXT:"fastest-spreading on record"]. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said "there is no evidence that it has gone into the communities" and that there was "no need for any panic", as health officials intensified contact tracing and monitoring of people who may have been exposed "This is a contained, single case and we are diligently working to ensure that it remains so," he said Pate said there was no reason at present to alter plans for large public gatherings, but left open the possibility of additional measures if the situation worsened "We have only one case, and hopefully it will stay that way," he said

item.title: El STOXX 600 europeo sufre su mayor caída en tres semanas por desplome de bancos y alza del crudo
item.description: El índice europeo STOXX 600 anotó el jueves su mayor caída en tres semanas, lastrado por la debilidad de las acciones bancarias, mientras que el alza de los precios del petróleo y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos franceses frenaron aún más el apetito por el riesgo.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: El índice europeo STOXX 600 anotó el jueves su mayor caída en tres semanas, lastrado por la debilidad de las acciones bancarias, mientras que el alza de los precios del petróleo y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos franceses frenaron aún más el apetito por el riesgo. * El índice paneuropeo (.STOXX) cerró con una caída superior al 1%, a 637,74 puntos. El índice bancario de la zona del euro (.SX7E) fue el de peor desempeño, con un descenso del 4,2%, lo que supuso su peor jornada desde marzo. * El español Bankinter (BKT.MC) cayó un 7,6% tras publicar sus resultados, que revelaron que el aumento de las tasas de interés incrementó los costos de los depósitos y ejerció presión sobre los márgenes en el tercer trimestre. * Barclays (BARC.L) cayó un 2,3% tras anunciar unos beneficios del tercer trimestre inferiores a lo esperado. El banco anunció que recortará este año unos 5.000 puestos de trabajo, lo que supone el 5% de su plantilla. * En general, los resultados empresariales europeos han sido sólidos, lo que en ocasiones ha ayudado a los inversionistas a hacer caso omiso de un panorama económico sombrío. Sin embargo, las caídas del jueves ponen de manifiesto lo rápido que puede deteriorarse la confianza cuando unos resultados decepcionantes chocan con la incertidumbre económica. * "Tenemos grandes preocupaciones en el mercado", dijo Joost van Leenders, estratega sénior de inversiones de Van Lanschot Kempen Investment Management, refiriéndose al conflicto de Oriente Medio que el jueves llevó a los futuros del crudo Brent a un máximo de cinco meses. * Además, el diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos franceses a 10 años y los bonos alemanes (Bunds) también alcanzó un nuevo máximo de 15 años en un contexto de incertidumbre política y protestas en Francia. * Hermes (HRMS.PA) cayó un 5% después de que el fabricante de los bolsos Birkin publicó unos ingresos trimestrales ligeramente inferiores a lo esperado, lo que lastró el índice de lujo (.STXLUXP) . * Nestlé (NESN.S) subió un 1,1% tras anunciar un crecimiento orgánico de las ventas en el tercer trimestre mejor de lo esperado. El índice de alimentación y bebidas (.SX3P) subió un 0,6%, uno de los pocos sectores que cerró al alza. * El índice tecnológico (.SX8P) volvió a sufrir presiones, siguiendo la tendencia de ventas masivas en el mundo, y cerró con una caída del 2%. Las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, como Infineon (IFXGn.DE) , STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) y ASML (ASML.AS) , cayeron entre un 5% y un 6%.

item.title: Penguins F Ben Kindel back in Pittsburgh after fainting on team plane
item.description: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after he was hospitalized in Salt Lake City and might even return to practice as soon as next week, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after he was hospitalized in Salt Lake City and might even return to practice as soon as next week, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday. Kindel, 19, had an urgent medical issue about 10 minutes after the team charter departed Salt Lake City International Airport on Tuesday, forcing the aircraft to turn around and land. Team medical staff cared for him until the plane was on the ground, at which time emergency medical technicians from a waiting ambulance took over. Dubas revealed that Kindel fainted due to a "vasovagal episode." He was given oxygen on the aircraft and regained consciousness. Formally called vasovagal syncope, it is "a common, generally benign type of fainting caused by a sudden drop in blood pressure and sometimes heart rate, which temporarily reduces blood flow to the brain," according to Johns Hopkins Medicine. It can be triggered by a variety of situations, including standing too long or prolonged exercise, per Johns Hopkins. "He's back in the building for treatment and testing today," Dubas said. "We'll place him on injured reserve and will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben. That's our primary goal." Doctors gave Kindel the OK to return to Pittsburgh on Wednesday. He was accompanied by the team staff members who remained in Utah with him. Pittsburgh was returning home from a four-game road trip that concluded Monday with a 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth. Kindel played 18:53 in the game and did not record a point. The 11th overall selection in the 2025 NHL Draft, Kindel is in his second season with Pittsburgh. He has two goals and two assists through nine games this season after totaling 17 goals and 18 assists in 77 games as a rookie. Kindel, a native of Coquitlam, British Columbia, made the Penguins out of training camp as an 18-year-old last season. Pittsburgh is scheduled to return to action Thursday when it hosts the Florida Panthers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Penguins, following positive news about Ben Kindel's condition, face off with Panthers
item.description: The Pittsburgh Penguins return to the ice against the visiting Florida Panthers on Thursday night, two days after a health scare involving Ben Kindel.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Penguins return to the ice against the visiting Florida Panthers on Thursday night, two days after a health scare involving Ben Kindel. The 19-year-old forward fainted on the team flight out of Salt Lake City on Tuesday. The flight returned to the airport, and Kindel was taken to the University of Utah Hospital for further evaluation. General manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday that Kindel suffered a case of vasovagal syncope. It is "a common, generally benign type of fainting caused by a sudden drop in blood pressure and sometimes heart rate, which temporarily reduces blood flow to the brain," according to Johns Hopkins Medicine. The Penguins canceled practice on Wednesday as they prepare to open a three-game homestand by hosting the Panthers, but they had to take the practice ice on Thursday with relief, knowing Kindel should be able to return to practice soon. The Panthers likely aren't as happy after seeing their three-game winning streak end with a 5-1 road loss against the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday. Brady Tkachuk scored and Akira Schmid made 25 saves for Florida. Tkachuk spent his first eight seasons in Ottawa before requesting and receiving a trade this summer. In his return, he gave the Panthers a 1-0 lead 10 minutes into the game. Tkachuk has 11 points (seven goals, four assists) in his past five games, including two natural hat tricks. The Panthers had scored 18 goals over their previous three games. With Thursday being the second of back-to-back games, it could mark the NHL debut of Florida goalie Cooper Black, who was recalled from Charlotte of the AHL with Jacob Markstrom out 10 to 14 days with an upper-body injury. Black, a 25-year-old Dartmouth product, joined the Panthers organization as an undrafted free agent in 2024 and signed a two-year, two-way contract extension in June. "He'll get some games," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. "He's been good. He's been good in practice. He looks like he fits. He looks comfortable. It's the right time for him to get in." At 6-foot-8, Black will become the tallest starting goaltender in NHL history when he makes his debut. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, is in a 1-6-1 rut since winning its first two games of the season. The Penguins just concluded an 0-4-0 road trip. On Monday night in Utah, Pittsburgh rallied from a 5-2 deficit to get within 5-4 on Declan Carlile's goal at 14:55 of the third period. However, the Penguins could not get the equalizer as Kindel's point-blank attempt was saved by Sebastian Cossa in the final minute. Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell each had a goal and an assist for the Penguins, and Bryan Rust recorded two assists. Arturs Silovs made 24 saves. The Penguins had scored three goals or fewer in each of their previous seven games. "My viewpoint is that we're facing some adversity right now," Muse said. "We have to stay together. We have to just be looking to make gains here each day, definitely each game and we have to make the way we play on the defensive side a priority and consistent." Karlsson has six points (two goals, four assists) in a four-game point streak. Rust left the game in the second period due to a lower-body injury after crashing awkwardly into the boards. He didn't return to action and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, head coach Dan Muse said Thursday. The Penguins swept three games from the Panthers last season. Captain Sidney Crosby had two goals and an assist in a 5-3 win on Oct. 23 in Sunrise, Fla. Evgeni Malkin accounted for three goals and an assist in a 9-4 rout on April 4 in Pittsburgh, and Rakell scored two goals and Crosby collected a goal and two assists in a 5-2 win the next day in Pittsburgh. --Field Level Media

item.title: Índice europeu STOXX 600 sofre maior queda em 3 semanas, com bancos em queda e petróleo em alta

item.content:encoded: O índice europeu STOXX 600 registrou nesta quinta-feira sua maior queda em três semanas, pressionado pela desvalorização das ações bancárias, enquanto os preços mais altos do petróleo e o aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos franceses reduziram o apetite por risco. Os resultados corporativos europeus têm sido, em geral, sólidos, às vezes ajudando os investidores a ignorar um cenário econômico sombrio. item.title: US railroads pull ahead as high fuel costs hit truckers harder
item.description: Record fuel prices are pushing freight off US highways and onto trains, helping railroad companies rake in higher revenue and profits as shippers look for cheaper ways to move goods long distances.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Gomes, Apratim Sarkar
item.content:encoded: Record fuel prices are pushing freight off US highways and onto trains, helping railroad companies rake in higher revenue and profits as shippers look for cheaper ways to move goods long distances. [USN:L4N46817V TEXT:"Union Pacific"] (UNP.N) , [USN:L4N4680RT TEXT:"Norfolk Southern"] (NSC.N) and [USN:L1N467138 TEXT:"CSX"] (CSX.O) all reported a jump in third-quarter profit and revenue this week, with company executives saying high fuel costs and fewer available trucks were sending more business their way. "Railroads are much more efficient. It costs us way less per ton to move products across the US. So when fuel prices go up, it's naturally an advantage," Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena told investors on a post-earnings call on Thursday. The shift gives railroads a chance to win back long-haul freight from trucks, though higher fuel prices are raising their own costs and squeezing margins as the Iran war keeps fuel prices elevated. Diesel, a key cost for freight carriers, [USN:L6N45N17X TEXT:"reached a record"] $6.53 per gallon in September, according to AAA data. Railroad gains are showing up most clearly in intermodal shipments, where freight is moved by rail for the long-haul portion of the journey, with trucks typically handling pickup and final delivery. Intermodal shipments compete directly with long-haul trucking. "We are seeing long-haul truckload shift to intermodal and increased use of transload and rail-served distribution centers," said James Mourafetis, head of transportation, logistics and services at consulting firm EFESO. Union Pacific's domestic intermodal volume rose 13% from a year earlier in the third quarter, while CSX reported a 7% rise and Norfolk Southern 3%. Shrinking trucking capacity is also moving some freight onto rail. A prolonged freight downturn has forced smaller carriers out of the market, with high operating costs and stricter driver enforcement limiting the return of trucking capacity. "The truck market has certainly flipped this year, but recent tonnage levels confirm this is due to reduced capacity, not robust demand," said American Trucking Associations' Chief Economist Bob Costello. However, higher fuel prices are also raising costs for railroads, making it harder to translate stronger revenue into higher profits, though fuel surcharges have offset some of that pressure. Union Pacific said high fuel prices hurt its third-quarter operating ratio by 140 basis points, while Norfolk Southern said fuel costs accounted for about half of the year-over-year increase in both revenue and expenses.

item.title: Top RFK Jr. adviser Calley Means quits Trump administration
item.description: Calley Means, a close aide to US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., is resigning from his role as a senior adviser in the Trump administration, he said in a post on X on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Calley Means, a close aide to US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., is resigning from his role as a senior adviser in the Trump administration, he said in a post on X on Thursday. Means, who has been particularly active in the Kennedy-led “Make America Healthy Again,” submitted his resignation to Kennedy on Wednesday, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters. "It was an honor to advocate for MAHA moms in the administration and steer policies like Dietary Guidelines reform, psychedelic reform, removing soda from SNAP, removing food dyes, GRAS reform, and overhauling government food procurement," Means said in his post on X. He added that he is resigning from the White House with "tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy." Means stepped into a [USN:L1N41D1B6 TEXT:"permanent role"] as senior adviser supporting food and nutrition policy in November last year. Before that, he served as an adviser in the Trump White House from March to October as a special government employee. The Wall Street Journal, which first reported his resignation earlier on Thursday, said Means was significantly frustrated by White House delays of some of Kennedy’s most popular policy ideas and blamed others in the administration for allowing food companies and special interests to have too much sway, citing people familiar with the matter. The Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. His sister, Casey Means, also a key ally of Health Secretary Kennedy, had her nomination for US surgeon general [USN:L1N41D1B6 TEXT:"withdrawn"] by President Donald Trump earlier this year.

item.title: Com apoio a Trump em queda, evangélicos brancos seguem como base sólida entre republicanos
item.description: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, está perdendo apoio entre muitos dos eleitores que o reelegeram para a Casa Branca em 2024. Mas pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos e entrevistas com cristãos evangélicos brancos mostram que eles continuam sendo seu eleitorado mais fiel e podem se revelar cruciais nas eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne, Julio-Cesar Chavez, Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, está perdendo apoio entre muitos dos eleitores que o reelegeram para a Casa Branca em 2024. Mas pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos e entrevistas com cristãos evangélicos brancos mostram que eles continuam sendo seu eleitorado mais fiel e podem se revelar cruciais nas eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro. Com os republicanos na defensiva em meio a índices de aprovação de Trump em níveis historicamente baixos, uma forte participação dos evangélicos poderia ajudar o partido a limitar as perdas causadas pela frustração dos eleitores com o custo de vida e a guerra contra o Irã. Essa lealdade ficou evidente na semana passada na Village Church, uma congregação evangélica em Blythewood, na Carolina do Sul, onde centenas de fiéis se reuniram para o sermão semanal “Bíblia e Política”, ministrado pelo pastor Erik Estep. O pano de fundo: uma disputa inesperadamente acirrada por uma vaga no Senado dos EUA, atualmente ocupada por um republicano. Falando no salão principal de culto, emoldurado por uma tela gigante de vídeo e iluminação no estilo de show, Estep não endossou nenhum candidato ou partido. Mas, ao se pronunciar contra o jogo, após sermões sobre aborto e socialismo, ele exortou seus fiéis — predominantemente brancos — a enxergarem a política por uma lente bíblica. “Acredito que a igreja é o baluarte da verdade para nossa nação”, disse Estep do palco. “E serão necessárias pessoas como vocês e igrejas como esta para proteger esta nação espiritual e moralmente.” A mensagem ressoou em Karen Whiting, uma executiva aposentada do setor farmacêutico de 72 anos que planeja votar na republicana Darline Graham em vez de Annie Andrews, a democrata. Graham foi nomeada pelo governador para ocupar a vaga de seu falecido irmão, o senador Lindsey Graham. Whiting citou preocupações de que os democratas permitam que meninas e mulheres transgênero participem de esportes femininos, ecoando outros evangélicos brancos entrevistados pela Reuters na Carolina do Sul na semana passada, que priorizaram questões sociais e religiosas em detrimento das preocupações econômicas. Andrews, no entanto, afirmou em um anúncio de campanha recente que se opõe à participação de mulheres transgênero em esportes femininos e às cirurgias de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade. “Estou votando em favor dos princípios bíblicos e não acredito que o Partido Democrata defenda esses princípios”, disse Whiting. “Sem Deus, este país está fadado ao fracasso.” Se os presentes na Village Church precisassem de orientações mais explícitas sobre como votar, um guia de candidatos disponível no saguão da igreja não deixava dúvidas. Produzido pelo grupo conservador cristão Palmetto Family Council e distribuído a igrejas em toda a Carolina do Sul, o guia atribuiu a Graham marcas de verificação verdes em todas as sete questões avaliadas, incluindo restrições à medicação abortiva e aos cuidados de afirmação de gênero, enquanto Andrews recebeu principalmente Xs vermelhos. Em um sinal da crescente competitividade da disputa pelo Senado, Trump fez campanha por Graham em um comício na noite de quarta-feira na Universidade de Clemson, na Carolina do Sul, concentrando grande parte de suas críticas em questões transgênero e acusando falsamente Andrews de apoiar a “mutilação sexual” de crianças. Andrews apresentou uma interpretação diferente das prioridades dos eleitores evangélicos. Em declaração à Reuters, ela disse ter visitado igrejas evangélicas e se encontrado com eleitores de várias religiões, orientações políticas e origens, constatando que a principal preocupação deles era a economia. “Eles estão enfrentando dificuldades com o custo de tudo. É por isso que estou concorrendo”, afirmou ela. LAÇOS FORTES Pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos mostram que o apoio a Trump entre os evangélicos brancos caiu para 63% neste mês, ante 77% em janeiro de 2025. A queda é ligeiramente menor do que a observada entre o eleitorado como um todo, de 47% para 31%, e os evangélicos brancos continuam sendo o único grande grupo demográfico monitorado pela Reuters/Ipsos em que seu apoio ultrapassa 60%. O vínculo de Trump, que já se casou três vezes, com os evangélicos brancos resistiu a uma década de escândalos e investigações, incluindo dezenas de alegações de conduta sexual imprópria — que ele nega — e um caso de pagamento para silenciar uma atriz pornô. A questão para os republicanos é se as pressões econômicas e a insatisfação com a guerra contra o Irã, agora em seu oitavo mês, estão enfraquecendo esse vínculo. Entrevistas da Reuters com 15 pessoas em duas igrejas da Carolina do Sul sugeriram que sua influência sobre os eleitores evangélicos brancos continuava forte. Na Village Church e na Carolina Baptist Church, na cidade de Spartanburg, a cerca de 90 minutos de carro de Blythewood, apenas 2 das 15 pessoas disseram estar considerando votar em Andrews, e nenhuma indicou que estava abandonando Trump. Embora vários tenham expressado frustração com o conflito com o Irã e o aumento dos preços da gasolina, a maioria disse confiar que Trump impedirá o Irã de obter uma arma nuclear ou, assim como Trump, atribuiu a inflação às políticas adotadas pelo presidente democrata Joe Biden. Chad Connelly, um ativista evangélico que lidera o grupo cristão de engajamento eleitoral Faith Wins, disse que, embora os evangélicos “não gostem de pagar preços mais altos”, eles se mobilizam igualmente por questões sociais. As preocupações com atletas transgêneros estão “realmente presentes em todos os lugares” nas quase duas dúzias de Estados que ele visitou neste ciclo eleitoral, afirmou. A lealdade dos evangélicos brancos a Trump reflete o que Robert P. Jones, presidente do Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) — uma organização sem fins lucrativos que estuda religião e política — chama de “grande acordo” forjado durante a eleição de 2016. Muitos evangélicos ignoraram sua conduta pessoal em troca de seu compromisso de restringir o aborto e os direitos LGBTQ, promover uma visão cristã conservadora da vida norte-americana e adotar políticas de imigração rígidas que alguns apoiadores veem como uma forma de preservar a identidade cristã branca do país, disse Jones. “Isso provou ser mais importante para esse grupo do que o que eles estão tendo que pagar no posto de gasolina”, disse Jones, que escreveu extensivamente sobre a ascensão do nacionalismo cristão na política norte-americana, à Reuters. POR QUE OS EVANGÉLICOS SÃO IMPORTANTES Os evangélicos brancos representam cerca de 13% dos adultos dos EUA, mas quase um terço da coalizão vencedora de Trump em 2024, de acordo com uma pesquisa do PRRI e uma análise de eleitores validados realizada pelo Pew Research Center, uma instituição apartidária. Mais de 80% votaram em Trump em cada uma de suas três campanhas presidenciais, segundo o Pew. Eles diferem acentuadamente dos evangélicos protestantes negros, que apoiam de forma esmagadora os democratas. A lealdade dos evangélicos também pode se mostrar decisiva nas disputas pelo Senado fora da Carolina do Sul, que podem ajudar a determinar o controle do Congresso, inclusive em Iowa e no Kansas, onde os evangélicos brancos representam uma parcela significativa do eleitorado. Pesquisas de opinião sugerem que a disputa na Carolina do Sul está acirrada. Nesta semana, o Trafalgar Group, uma empresa de pesquisa com tendência republicana, divulgou uma pesquisa mostrando Andrews 3 pontos percentuais atrás de Graham. Parte do desafio de Graham decorre do mal-estar persistente entre alguns conservadores em relação à sua indicação para a vaga no Senado. Mesmo após receber o apoio de Trump, a novata na política derrotou por uma margem estreita o deputado federal Ralph Norman no segundo turno do partido, em agosto, o que reforçou as dúvidas de alguns republicanos sobre sua experiência e suas credenciais conservadoras. Um porta-voz da campanha de Graham não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. No entanto, mesmo evangélicos pouco entusiasmados com Graham, como Kevin Thomas, de 53 anos, disseram sentir que tinham poucas opções. Thomas, que participou do sermão na Village Church e apoiou Norman, afirmou que, mesmo assim, não confiava em Andrews em questões relacionadas a pessoas transgênero. “Estou inclinado a tapar o nariz e votar em Graham”, disse Thomas. “Não estou disposto a sacrificar seis anos tendo uma democrata nos representando na Carolina do Sul.”

item.title: French bond pain puts euro zone's weak links on notice
item.description: As a selloff in French government bonds deepens, the region's debt-laden economies risk a surge in borrowing costs while also grappling with increasing social unrest.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Cooper, Dhara Ranasinghe
item.content:encoded: As a selloff in French government bonds deepens, the region's debt-laden economies risk a surge in borrowing costs while also grappling with increasing social unrest. French 10-year bond yields on Thursday hit a [USN:L6N4680QK TEXT:"fresh 24-year high above 5%"], driving their premium over benchmark German Bunds to nearly 180 basis points , or 1.8%, the most since the depths of the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. A huge fiscal deficit that has been complicated by political stalemate in Paris and the [USN:L6N4680S7 TEXT:"worst civil unrest in years"] are the latest catalysts. As France has come under strain, investors are turning up the heat on the likes of Italy, Belgium and even Greece. Similar to France, students took to the streets in Belgium at the weekend to protest against high housing costs, while Italy has also faced protests. Italian yields have risen 14 bps this week to 4.616%, not far off early October's three-year highs. The premium Belgium pays to borrow over 10 years relative to Germany rose to its highest in 14 years at 109 bps . "Markets look ahead and they say 'well, if borrowing costs stay this high, then eventually you're going to have to refinance at higher rates'," said Mike Bell, head of market strategy at BlueBay Asset Management. While he does not expect the gap between French and German bond yields to get as wide as those of Italy and Spain against Germany during the euro debt crisis, which hit 6% and 5% then, respectively, it could exceed 2%. Bell said concern that French politicians would shy away from taking the necessary steps to put France on a sustainable debt path, especially given the protests, could heighten pressure. TAKE OUT SOME INSURANCE Belgium's debt yields have risen steadily this year along with those elsewhere given rising energy prices, but that rise has accelerated. Its 10-year borrowing costs rose by as much as 12 bps on Thursday to 4.54%, the highest since early 2012. Highlighting the unease, the cost of insuring against the risk of default for Belgium hit its highest since April 2020 on Thursday at nearly 39 basis points. This is well below the levels logged during the euro zone debt crisis in 2012, but the speed at which Belgian CDS have risen rivals that of France, with both having more than doubled in the last month. "Belgium's had a lot of debt for a long time," Chris Scicluna, head of research at Daiwa Capital Markets, said. "It obviously has a history of political paralysis and government paralysis and if you've got a deficit that needs to be reduced, sadly, over the years, that's not helpful," he said. "So, it does tick a lot of the boxes that should leave investors uneasy, but certainly, it's not France." Italian bonds have performed strongly in recent years, bringing their yields below those of France last September for the first time since the debt crisis. They, too, are back in the spotlight. An election next year [USN:L8N45Z1S1 TEXT:"throws doubt on Rome's"] plans to reverse the rise in its huge public debt, analysts say. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni approved tough anti-riot measures after unrest swept northern Italian cities at the weekend, including [USN:L8N4661X4 TEXT:"financial capital Milan"]. "Fuel prices, widespread cost-of-living pressures and housing prices continue to top the list of grievances, underlining the point that while many developed economies continue to show considerable resilience, there is little or no 'feel-good factor' for the majority of the public at large," ASM Investor Services global economist Marc Ostwald said.

item.title: Former Euroleague CEO warns clubs against surrendering control to NBA
item.description: Former Euroleague CEO Jordi Bertomeu told Reuters on Thursday that the competition's clubs should not give up control over their future in any collaboration with the NBA's planned European league.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Former Euroleague CEO Jordi Bertomeu told Reuters on Thursday that the competition's clubs should not give up control over their future in any collaboration with the NBA's planned European league. The NBA is targeting October 2027 for the launch of NBA Europe, while Euroleague plans to expand its competition for the 2027-28 season. Euroleague CEO Chus Bueno told Reuters on Monday that further fragmentation of European basketball would be "[USN:L6N4650V6 TEXT:"a disaster"]", although both sides say they remain open to working together. Bertomeu told Reuters that collaboration was in everyone's interests, but the NBA's current offer was not attractive to Euroleague. Euroleague's 13 shareholder clubs collectively own and govern the competition, giving them a say over its format, financial model and strategic direction. The NBA proposal has not been made public, but Bertomeu said its terms "as they are being presented today are not those of a collaboration, based on what we know." The Euroleague shareholders rejected the proposal at a meeting on October 6. Earlier this month a senior executive at a Euroleague club told Reuters that they expected the NBA to come back with an improved offer. Euroleague and NBA Europe have both promised growth for the 13 Euroleague shareholder clubs. Bueno says most Euroleague clubs would be sustainable within five years under its [USN:L6N4620ST TEXT:"10-year business plan"], while NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum told Reuters on Tuesday that the NBA Europe model promised a "[USN:L6N45U0IB TEXT:"much quicker path to profitability"]". Tatum added that the NBA was "prepared to proceed regardless" of whether the Euroleague collaborated on its NBA Europe project. Asked about Tatum's comments, Bertomeu, 67, warned that the path to improved economic results for shareholder clubs was no clearer under the NBA model. "If European clubs move to a model that they are told will generate much more economic activity and much higher revenues, it is not guaranteed." Bertomeu said the potential trade-off could not be measured solely in financial terms. "In exchange, they would give up control over their own future. And if, three years from now, what they have been promised does not happen, they will not be able to change anything," he said. "In 26 years (of Euroleague), I was there for 22. During those 22 years we made mistakes, but we had the ability to correct them. We decided to change course and made our own decisions. (In NBA Europe) that would no longer be the case." NBA sources told Reuters on Thursday that all shareholding clubs would participate in league governance, just as they do in the NBA. Bertomeu led Euroleague Basketball from its creation in 2000 until stepping down in 2022. He said the NBA could make its biggest contribution to the growth of Euroleague clubs in commercial operations and stadium infrastructure. "I have no doubt that the NBA could do an extraordinary commercial job. That is where the NBA could do great things. "I believe these should be the points of collaboration between the two parties," said Bertomeu, adding that format changes and economic reform were unnecessary.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s designated first citizen
item.description: The Facebook founder doesn’t hide his admiration for Roman Emperor Augustus. An agreement allows him to sell new non-voting stock to pay a tax bill. Doing so, gives him a larger purse to pursue bigger dreams of conquest while retaining absolute control. Caveat emptor applies.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cyran
item.content:encoded: Mark Zuckerberg has never hidden his obsession with Rome and emperor Augustus. A new agreement keeps Meta Platforms’ (META.O) first citizen in the $1.8 trillion company’s capital of Menlo Park, California for eight years. It also allows the founder, chairman and chief executive to pursue bigger dreams of conquest while retaining absolute control. Zuckerberg has some 60% of the company's vote because of Class B shares, which have 10 votes a piece. Yet his economic stake is far less at around 14%. A proposed California tax would hit billionaires like Zuckerberg for 5% of their wealth. He told Meta’s board he might move out of the Golden State, according to the New York Times. It’s understandable directors want the boss in California. Under his leadership, the Facebook and Instagram operator has grown from start up to one of the most valuable companies on earth. Zuckerberg’s focus may be on Meta’s big push into artificial intelligence, but having a leader around the office still delivers better results according to a study by researchers at Boston College and Arizona State University. The company will issue one non-voting Class C share for each existing share investors have. Zuckerberg can sell up to 20% of his immediately, and the remainder in steps, without reducing his voting power. In exchange he stays put instead of relocating out of state. It’s not obvious that Zuckerberg would actually move, let alone leave the company. His desire for retaining power reflects his care for the entity he built. The new shares will be useful for many things. Meta can use them to buy rivals, compensate workers, or raise money to invest in data centers. The company will need this ability, as its artificial intelligence push chews up resources. On Wednesday, the company said it burned over $2 billion in cash in the third quarter. Shareholders have revolted before. In 2017 the company abandoned an attempt to issue non-voting stock. What’s different today is the expensive race to dominate machine learning. Perhaps the opportunity is so big, and the increasing number of tech giants with non-voting stock like SpaceX (SPCX.O) , that equity owners will play along. Rome’s history, though, is hardly an endorsement of letting one person hold absolute power. If things start to go wrong, Meta’s ruler can essentially ignore plebeian investors. Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky . Meta Platforms said on October 21 that the board had approved a new class of non-voting stock. All Class A and B owners would be issued one new Class C share for each share held. Founder, Chief Executive and Chair Mark Zuckerberg agreed to a deal wherein he can sell up to 20% of his Class C shares in exchange for a commitment to stay in California and remain head of the company for eight years. If he sells more of the shares, his voting stake will be reduced. The restriction on his remaining Class C shares will be lifted in steps over this period. Zuckerberg has a 60% voting stake and owns just over 13% of all shares. The company also reported third quarter results on October 21. In the three months ending September 30, the company had $2.1 billion of negative free cash flow. Meta’s stock fell 6% in early trading on the morning of October 22. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Trump says LeBron James showed disrespect during US national anthem
item.description: US President Donald Trump criticized NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the singing of the national anthem at a recent NBA game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump criticized NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the singing of the national anthem at a recent NBA game. "While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country," Trump said in a Truth Social post accompanied by a video showing James moving his body during the singing of the anthem. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" The clip Trump shared showed James standing in line with the members of the Philadelphia 76ers, swinging his arms in a warmup-type stretch and performing basketball shooting movements. A representative for the 76ers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump has repeatedly criticized athletes for their behavior during pre-game renditions of the US national anthem, notably beginning with NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick's kneeling protest in support of racial justice. Trump canceled a planned White House visit of the Super Bowl champions Philadelphia Eagles in 2018 after the team disagreed with his call for players to stand during the anthem. James became a leading voice in the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020 and has [USN:L1N34L0CT TEXT:"frequently supported"] progressive issues as he ascended to the top of the NBA's all-time scoring list.

item.title: Trump ordered to sit for deposition in his $10 billion BBC lawsuit
item.description: A federal judge on Thursday ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by December 11 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath.
item.dc:creator: Jack Queen
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Thursday ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by December 11 in his $10 billion [USN:L1N3WQ18J TEXT:"defamation lawsuit"] against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath. Trump is suing Britain’s publicly funded broadcaster for at least $10 billion over a [USN:S8N3TC0DO TEXT:"misleadingly edited"] clip of a speech. The case is one of several Trump has privately filed against the news media as part of a wider [USN:L6N40Z025 TEXT:"pressure campaign"] against [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"coverage he dislikes"]. US Magistrate Judge Enjolique Lett ordered Trump to take questions from the BBC’s lawyers under oath in a ruling from the bench at a court hearing on Thursday, according to a spokesman for Trump's personal legal team. Trump canceled a deposition in October, citing conflicts with his presidential duties. The Trump spokesman said the lawsuit is aimed at holding the BBC accountable for defamation and “reckless election interference.” The BBC declined to comment. It previously admitted the edits were misleading and apologized to Trump, though it denies being liable for defamation. Trump’s lawsuit filed in December in Florida federal court accuses the BBC of intentionally misleading viewers into thinking he directed supporters to storm the US Capitol by splicing together different parts of a January 6, 2021, speech. In court filings, the broadcaster has accused Trump and his lawyers of dragging their feet in response to their requests for records and other information that is exchanged between parties in a process known as discovery. The BBC is seeking financial records from Trump's Mar-a-Lago club and the web of business entities associated with him, saying the information is necessary to defend against Trump’s damages claims. Trump’s lawyers say the requests are too broad and irrelevant to the case. They have also denied in court filings that Trump is avoiding a deposition, saying Trump's duties and security needs must take precedence. The edited speech appeared in a BBC "Panorama" documentary show shortly before the 2024 presidential election, which Trump won. A leaked internal BBC memo cited the edits as evidence of potential political bias, sparking a public relations crisis for the broadcaster and leading to high-level resignations.

item.title: L'Oreal Q3 sales beat forecasts as consumers indulge in premium beauty
item.description: French cosmetics group L'Oreal beat third-quarter sales forecasts on Thursday, as shoppers around the world indulge in more pricy haircare and premium skin products.
item.dc:creator: Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: French cosmetics group L'Oreal (OREP.PA) beat third-quarter sales forecasts on Thursday, as shoppers around the world indulge in more pricy haircare and premium skin products. The Paris-based maker of CeraVe moisturiser and Prada perfumes has doubled down on its premium offer in recent years, adding more couture perfumes to its stable of blockbuster names and rolling out new haircare products under its professional hair salon brand Kerastase. Its weight in both segments is allowing it to profit from growing global spending on beauty, including in China where demand for higher-end brands is accelerating. Sales from July to September rose 7.7% on an adjusted like-for-like basis to €11.56 billion ($12.95 billion), topping analysts' consensus forecast for 5.9% growth in a Visible Alpha poll. The number strips out currency effects and the effects from phasing in of a new global IT system. "The global beauty market, once again, proved its resilience in a challenging context — and we continued to significantly outpace it," CEO Nicolas Hieronimus said in a statement. L'Oreal's US-listed shares rose 8.3% after the sales report. Beauty has been a bright spot in an otherwise sluggish consumer goods sector, with analysts and executives pointing to the "lipstick effect" of consumers treating themselves to affordable luxuries during challenging times. L'Oreal's luxury division, which generates more than a third of group revenue, grew 7% on a like-for-like basis, well ahead of a 4.5% forecast, helped by strong demand for its best-selling fragrances like Prada Paradigme and for high-end skincare in China. China's beauty market is expanding again after two years of contraction, as middle-class consumers shift spending from entry-level luxury goods towards [USN:L6N44008X TEXT:"prestige beauty"] products. Growth slowed slightly in the third quarter against a tougher base of comparison than earlier in the year, Hieronimus told analysts on a call, but some brands like Helena Rubinstein are growing in 'high double-digits'. "Our products are more affordable than higher-priced luxury and consumers are indulging in them," he said. Other skincare lines like SkinCeuticals and La Roche-Posay which has launched new sunscreen and serums are also growing in double-digits, he added, while the company is also targeting consumers using [USN:L4N45K10K TEXT:"GLP-1 weight-loss drugs"], promoting products aimed at addressing secondary effects such as sagging facial skin. Sales in Europe, L'Oreal's biggest market, rose nearly 9%, while revenue in South Asia and the Middle East jumped 19.5% on strong demand in Gulf countries and Vietnam. Shares in L'Oreal, France's most valuable listed company, are up 11% this year. ($1 = 0.8927 euros)

item.title: Rhode Island sues Meta over alleged tolerance for scam advertising
item.description: Rhode Island sued Meta Platforms in state court on Thursday over the company's alleged tolerance for widespread scam advertising on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Horwitz, Katie Paul
item.content:encoded: Rhode Island sued Meta Platforms (META.O) in state court on Thursday over the company's alleged tolerance for widespread scam advertising on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms. The suit, filed by Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha in Providence Superior Court, accuses Meta of unlawfully profiting from and participating in the creation of billions of dollars in scam advertising – even as it assured its billions of users that it was working diligently to protect them. It is the first such scams-related case to be brought against Meta by a US state, following a [USN:L1N41O010 TEXT:"similar lawsuit"] filed in May by California's Santa Clara County. The complaint seeks monetary civil penalties for each of Meta's alleged violations of Rhode Island state law, restitution to consumers, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains and a judicial order requiring the company to address, rather than profit from, scam ads it develops and delivers on its platforms. "As alleged, Meta knowingly exposed vulnerable users to fraud and scams, and made enormous profits in doing so. When companies, big or small, take advantage of Rhode Island consumers, this office will do everything within our authority to hold them to account," Neronha said in a press release. Meta said it would fight the lawsuit, calling it "unfounded," and noting that the company regularly partners with law enforcement to disrupt scam networks. "The attorney general refused to engage with us on ways we protect Rhode Islanders from scams, and has instead hired an out-of-state private law firm to concoct a lawsuit that ignores the full range of actions we take to combat scams every day," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said in a statement. Stone noted that Meta has removed more than 159 million scam ads and launched new anti-fraud tools in the past year alone, like alerts flagging suspicious friend requests on Facebook, expanded advertiser verification and warnings about risky device-linking requests on WhatsApp. HIGH-RISK SCAM ADS The suit was filed a day after a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay that state $25 billion in a case in which [USN:L6N45F10O TEXT:"a jury found"] the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data. Meta also agreed in August to [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"pay up to $18 billion"] in a settlement with nearly all US states to resolve claims it designed its platforms to addict children. Rhode Island's complaint cites Reuters reporting from last year on internal Meta documents outlining the vast scale of fraudulent advertising on the company's platforms – and Meta's calculations that it was earning far more from high-risk scam ads than it expected to pay in fines for allowing them. According to those documents, Meta displays around 15 billion "higher risk" scam ads to users every day, and earned roughly 10% of its 2024 revenue from fraudulent e-commerce, dubious health products and other banned marketing. In many cases, Rhode Island's suit alleged, Meta's AI ad creation tools actively assisted scammers with their fraudulent marketing. Rather than consistently blocking advertisers that its automated detection systems suspected of fraud, Rhode Island alleged, Meta sometimes charged them extra as a penalty. "Meta knowingly helped create and optimize these ads to ensure that they were as effective as possible and then lied about them, misrepresenting to the public its commitment to prevent fraud on its platforms," the suit stated. The company has disputed the Reuters reporting. "We aggressively fight fraud and scams because people on our platforms don't want this content, legitimate advertisers don't want it and we don't want it either," Stone said in response to the reporting last year, calling it "a selective view that distorts Meta's approach to fraud and scams." In the months since Reuters published the stories, Meta has claimed progress on anti-scam initiatives. At a White House [USN:L6N46618F TEXT:"event on cybercrime prevention"] on Wednesday, US Attorney General Todd Blanche called the company an "incredible partner to law enforcement." But Rhode Island alleged that scams remain rampant and readily findable in the company's ad library, a database of ads run on Meta's platforms. "The ad below, for example, promised to reverse Alzheimer's in 45 days," Rhode Island's complaint stated of one set of scam ads. "There were more than 2,000 versions of this ad active in the Meta Ad library." TARGETING THE ELDERLY Often the fraudulent ads targeted elderly people, Rhode Island alleged, citing an investigation by the nonprofit Center for Countering Digital Hate, which identified nearly 94,000 scam ads on Meta's platforms. "Some of these advertisers spent more on Meta ads over a several year period than large brands like Walmart or Pfizer," the lawsuit stated. Beyond scams, the Rhode Island attorney general's office said it found that Meta was similarly failing to police other types of illicit ads, such as for AI apps for deepfake pornography. In one example provided by the state, an ad featured side-by-side images of a fully clothed woman in a coffee shop next to an image of her engaged in a sex act. Rhode Island also cited examples of scam ads impersonating public figures and trusted institutions like banks to leverage their credibility, including a case in which scammers in China used the name and image of a senior Bank of America executive in ads on Facebook and Instagram that lured users into scam stock trades on WhatsApp. Public survey data cited by Rhode Island – and Meta's own internal appraisals obtained by Reuters – indicate that the company's platforms are responsible for a disproportionate share of online scams and that Meta's scam defenses were weaker than those of its main digital advertising competitors. "It is easier to advertise scams on Meta platforms than Google," concluded an internal Meta review in April 2025. Meta nonetheless sought to defeat regulatory efforts to require verification, Rhode Island said. The lawsuit stated that "a banned advertiser can reappear in the time it takes to provide a new email address or phone number."

item.title: Rendimiento bonos Tesoro EEUU se hunde ya que resurgen temores sobre sostenibilidad del auge de la IA
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos se hundió el jueves, ante una liquidación del mercado bursátil por renovadas preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad de las perspectivas de la inteligencia artificial, lo que potenció el atractivo de la deuda pública como valor de refugio.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos se hundió el jueves, ante una liquidación del mercado bursátil por renovadas preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad de las perspectivas de la inteligencia artificial, lo que potenció el atractivo de la deuda pública como valor de refugio. * El Nasdaq se desplomaba más de un 2%, mientras que las acciones de Meta (META.O) perdían casi un 8% tras la publicación de los resultados trimestrales de la empresa y el anuncio de nuevos valores sin derecho a voto destinados a financiar la expansión de la empresa de redes sociales en el ámbito de la IA. * Los retornos han bajado en los últimos días, ya que las preocupaciones sobre una desaceleración del gasto en IA y su impacto en el crecimiento económico han eclipsado los datos económicos, que mostraban presiones inflacionarias persistentes. * Los inversores ya habían descontado la inflación y la perspectiva de alzas de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal, pero los cambios en los activos de riesgo y en las condiciones financieras están impulsando ahora la demanda de bonos, según Thomas Urano, de Sage Advisory en Austin, Texas. * "La batalla entre las preocupaciones por la energía y la inflación y la demanda de refugio en los bonos del Tesoro lleva tiempo en marcha, pero en la última semana vemos quién está ganando ahora. La tendencia de 'huida hacia la calidad' está ganando terreno en el mercado de los bonos del Tesoro", señaló. * El rendimiento de la deuda referencial a 10 años cayó 19,3 puntos básicos (pb), al 4,953%, en su mayor descenso diario desde el 10 de marzo de 2023. Tocó el 7 de octubre su nivel más alto desde abril de 2002, al 5,3645%. * El retorno de las notas a 30 años restó 15 pb, al 5,287%, su retroceso diario más pronunciado desde agosto de 2024, mientras que el de los papeles a dos años , que suele moverse en línea con las expectativas de tasas de la Fed, se hundió 18,5 pb, al 4,638%, su mayor descenso en un día desde agosto de 2025. * Pese a los recientes datos que apuntan a un alza de la presión sobre los precios, los mercados descartan una subida de tasas de la Fed la próxima semana. La probabilidad de un aumento de al menos 25 pb se ha hundido al 7,2%, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, frente al 27,7% de hace una semana y el 55,4% de un mes atrás.

item.title: FIFA opens bidding for 2030 and 2034 World Cup media rights covering US and Puerto Rico
item.description: FIFA launched an invitation to tender on Thursday for media rights in the United States and Puerto Rico for the 2030 World Cup along with an option to secure the 2034 edition.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FIFA launched an invitation to tender on Thursday for media rights in the United States and Puerto Rico for the 2030 World Cup along with an option to secure the 2034 edition. FIFA said in a press release that it is open to "innovative approaches" to reach large audiences and that the bid submission deadline is November 19. Fox held the exclusive English-language broadcast rights in the United States for the 2026 World Cup co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico while Telemundo held the Spanish language rights. Spain, which won the 2026 World Cup, will co-host the 2030 edition with Portugal and Morocco, although Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will stage inaugural matches marking the tournament's 100th anniversary. Saudi Arabia have been named hosts of the 2034 World Cup. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup averaged 13.5 million viewers per match on linear and streaming platforms in the United States, up 166% on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Earlier this week, [USN:L6N45Z0QE TEXT:"Netflix"] announced that it secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Andorra.

item.title: Kering-Le recul des ventes de Gucci au T3 pèse sur les espoirs de relance
item.description: Le groupe de luxe français Kering a annoncé jeudi une baisse des ventes de Gucci au troisième trimestre, la faiblesse persistante de la fréquentation de ses magasins compliquant les efforts de redressement engagés par son directeur général Luca de Meo.
item.dc:creator: Tassilo Hummel, Alessandro Parodi, Elena Smirnova
item.content:encoded: Le groupe de luxe français Kering (PRTP.PA) a annoncé jeudi une baisse des ventes de Gucci au troisième trimestre, la faiblesse persistante de la fréquentation de ses magasins compliquant les efforts de redressement engagés par son directeur général Luca de Meo. [USN:L8N40Z0D8 TEXT:"Luca de Meo"], vétéran de l'industrie automobile qui a pris les rênes du groupe l'an dernier, tente de redresser Kering à travers un plan stratégique sur cinq ans visant à doubler sa marge opérationnelle. Mais les tensions au Moyen-Orient, la faiblesse de la demande en Chine et le ralentissement de la dynamique de consommation aux États-Unis compliquent la réalisation de cet objectif. Les ventes trimestrielles inférieures aux attentes publiées récemment par [USN:L8N45Y1DP TEXT:"LVMH"] et [USN:L8N4680BW TEXT:"Hermès"], ainsi que les signes d'un ralentissement de la demande aux États-Unis, ont renforcé les inquiétudes des investisseurs quant au redressement de Kering. Interrogée lors d'une conférence téléphonique sur la possibilité d'un retour à la croissance du groupe cette année, la directrice financière Armelle Poulou n'a pas souhaité commenter les perspectives, renvoyant à la publication des résultats annuels. Les certificats américains de dépôt (ADR) de Kering ont chuté de 11% après la publication de l'activité trimestrielle du groupe. Les ventes de Gucci, qui représentent environ la moitié du résultat opérationnel du groupe, se sont établies à 1,29 milliard d'euros au cours du trimestre. Sur l'ensemble du groupe, le chiffre d'affaires a reculé de 1% à données comparables. Selon Kering, la principale difficulté de Gucci reste la baisse de la fréquentation des magasins, particulièrement en Chine. Les ventes de la marque ont également légèrement reculé en Amérique du Nord. Pour attirer davantage de clients dans les magasins Gucci, Kering prévoit d'accroître ses investissements dans le marketing et l'expérience client, a déclaré Armelle Poulou. "Nous poursuivons l'exécution de notre plan avec la plus grande discipline", a déclaré Armelle Poulou. Elle a ajouté que le groupe avait déjà réduit son réseau de distribution de 105 magasins et anticipait désormais au moins 125 fermetures nettes sur l’exercice 2026. PRESSION SUR DEMNA Kering a nommé l'an dernier Luca de Meo pour restructurer le groupe. Après une hausse initiale à l'annonce de son arrivée, le titre Kering a perdu de son élan. L'action affiche un recul d'environ 8% sur un an, dans un contexte de repli plus général du secteur du luxe. Luca de Meo vise à doubler la marge opérationnelle de Kering d'ici à la fin de la décennie, à partir d'un niveau de 11,1% en 2025, grâce à des réductions de coûts, à de nouvelles fermetures de magasins et à une rationalisation de la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Des analystes estiment toutefois que ces seules mesures d'efficacité ne suffiront pas à relancer des marques qui ont perdu de leur attrait. Le directeur artistique de Saint Laurent, [USN:L8N45V0BG TEXT:"Anthony Vaccarello"], et [USN:FWN4611AW TEXT:"Sean McGirr"], d'Alexander McQueen, ont tous deux quitté leurs fonctions ce mois-ci. Les médias spécialisés spéculent également sur l'avenir de Pierpaolo Piccioli, directeur artistique de Balenciaga. Ces changements devraient accentuer encore la pression sur Demna, qui s'apprête à boucler sa première année complète à la tête de Gucci, qu'il a cherché à relancer en misant sur une esthétique audacieuse et sensuelle rappelant les succès de la marque sous Tom Ford. Demna a également adopté une approche inhabituelle en matière de production, en délocalisant en Chine la fabrication de ses premiers modèles de baskets.

item.title: Arizona university suspends fraternity after rape allegation
item.description: The University of Arizona has suspended a fraternity after a female student alleged she was raped at its house by two men, the latest action taken by a major US university against a Greek chapter over accusations of sexual assault.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hay
item.content:encoded: The University of Arizona has suspended a fraternity after a female student alleged she was raped at its house by two men, the latest action taken by a major US university against a Greek chapter over accusations of sexual assault. The university suspended Sigma Phi Epsilon, which was already on probation for hazing new members, on Wednesday after the KOLD-TV station reported the allegations of a female student who said she was raped at the chapter's fraternity house in Tucson. The university said it was investigating. "It has been determined that your organization presents a substantial risk to members of the university community," Whitney Mohr, associate dean of students, said in a letter to the fraternity. The female student told police she was at the Sigma Phi Epsilon fraternity house with friends and residents of the chapter around midnight on August 26 when she woke up in a dark room being sexually assaulted by two men, according to the September police report published by KOLD-TV. Sigma Phi Epsilon's national CEO Brian Warren said it took courage for the student to come forward, that she deserves a complete investigation, and that the fraternity does not tolerate sexual assault or sexual misconduct. "The fraternity has suspended the membership of those involved while the investigation proceeds," Warren said in a statement. "Any member found responsible will be expelled, and we will cooperate fully with law enforcement as it seeks accountability under the law." US universities have come under growing pressure to crack down on misconduct following allegations of sexual assault by fraternity members at [USN:L6N45Z16I TEXT:"Cornell University"]. Earlier this month, the University of Arizona suspended all fraternity activities during investigations into alleged hazing, physical assault and drug and alcohol violations.

item.title: External evaluators find flaws in OpenAI's AI monitoring system in pilot review
item.description: AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year. The exercise, conducted from July 21 to August 11, gave outside researchers "a deep level of access" to OpenAI's internal infrastructure for so-called embedded evaluations, the safety nonprofits said on Thursday. METR and Redwood said they each sent one researcher, tested an arrangement giving access to OpenAI's internal code, documentation and some technical staff. Both were accompanied on site and used OpenAI-issued devices that "never left the premises". OpenAI told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes. AI labs, experts and the Trump administration have touted independent evaluation by outside reviewers as a way to safely advance the technology without slowing its development.
