However, AI companies are worried that evaluator staff working inside the companies' walls could take proprietary information to rivals, Reuters [USN:L1N45S0TG TEXT:"reported"] earlier this month. While OpenAI received a full 61-page internal report, METR and Redwood said they agreed to publish only a broad summary publicly, and gave OpenAI the right to redact sensitive information. Unlike in some previous evaluations, they could not independently disclose those redactions, but said they expected greater transparency in future evaluations. The researchers also identified a potential way for OpenAI's Codex agents to bypass security restrictions and act with their users' full permissions. The evaluators assessed the monitoring system as it existed on and before July 21, and noted that OpenAI was expanding the system during the exercise. OpenAI said the "findings helped strengthen safeguards as we expanded the system and will help shape future research collaborations with METR and other third-party evaluators."

item.title: US to host inaugural Women's Club World Cup in 2028
item.description: The United States will host the inaugural edition of the Women's Club World Cup in January 2028, FIFA said on Thursday, with seven clubs confirmed so far for the 19-team tournament.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States will host the inaugural edition of the Women's Club World Cup in January 2028, FIFA said on Thursday, with seven clubs confirmed so far for the 19-team tournament. Arsenal Women, Club America Femenil, FC Barcelona Femeni, Gotham FC, Naegohyang Women’s FC, SC Corinthians and Wuhan Jiangda WFC have already qualified, with a dozen more yet to be determined. The tournament will feature teams from all six confederations -- three clubs apiece from AFC, CAF, CONCACAF and CONMEBOL, one from OFC and six from UEFA. It will run from January 5 to 30. "We undertook a detailed assessment to identify the most suitable host for the inaugural edition of the FIFA Women’s Club World Cup," FIFA Chief Women’s Football Officer Sarai Bareman said in a statement. "Ultimately, the United States’ recent excellence in staging top FIFA tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women’s football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option." FIFA has been eager to tap into the lucrative [USN:L6N43I00P TEXT:"American market"], and the US staged the men's Club World Cup in 2025 and co-hosted the FIFA World Cup earlier this year with Mexico and Canada. The United States is expected to co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico, with formal FIFA approval due next month.

item.title: Gucci sales slip again in latest blow to Kering recovery plan
item.description: Gucci sales fell in the third quarter as shoppers stayed away from its stores, its owner Kering said on Thursday, blowing hopes of a rapid return to growth for Luca de Meo, who took over as CEO last year.
item.dc:creator: Tassilo Hummel, Alessandro Parodi
item.content:encoded: Gucci sales fell in the third quarter as shoppers stayed away from its stores, its owner Kering (PRTP.PA) said on Thursday, blowing hopes of a rapid return to growth for Luca de Meo, who took over as CEO last year. The former automotive industry veteran is trying to turn Kering around with a five-year plan to double its profit margin, but the Iran war, weak demand in China and slowing momentum in the [USN:L8N45R16S TEXT:"United States"] are frustrating that ambition. Lower-than-expected quarterly sales at [USN:L6N45Y0VL TEXT:"LVMH"] (LVMH.PA) and [USN:L6N4680E3 TEXT:"Hermes"] (HRMS.PA) have added to investor concerns over Kering and asked on media call if returning to overall growth was still the aim this year, its finance chief Armelle Poulou declined to comment, pointing to the publication of full-year results. Kering's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were down 11% following its trading update, which showed sales at Gucci, which accounts for roughly half of group profit, were down 6% when adjusted for currency moves to €1.29 billion ($1.44 billion) in the quarter, while group revenue fell 1%. Footfall, in particular in China, is the main problem at Gucci, where sales have been falling for more than three years, Kering said. Gucci sales also slid slightly in North America. Kering plans to ramp up spending on marketing and client experience to attract more shoppers, Poulou said. "We keep on carrying out our plan with the utmost discipline," Poulou said, adding Kering has so far reduced its retail network by 105 stores and was targeting 125 closures by the end of the year. PRESSURE ON DESIGNER DEMNA Kering last year tapped De Meo to overhaul the group. Its shares had an early price bounce under the former Renault chief before cooling off, with the stock down 8% from a year earlier amid a wider sector downturn. [USN:S8N3SZ01C TEXT:"De Meo"] aims to double Kering's profit margin from 11.1% in 2025 by the end of the decade through cost cuts, more store closures and a push to streamline supply chains. But analysts have said mere efficiency measures will not be enough to turn around a business whose brands have lost appeal. Both [USN:L6N45V0BJ TEXT:"Anthony Vaccarello"], the creative director of its second-biggest brand Saint Laurent, and Alexander McQueen designer [USN:L6N46114V TEXT:"Sean McGirr"] left their posts this month. Fashion industry media have also speculated about the future of Balenciaga's creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli. The recent changes are likely to pile even more pressure on Demna, who is nearing his first full year at the helm of Gucci, which he sought to reignite with a bold bet on daring, sexy styles reminiscent of the brand's successes under Tom Ford. Demna also took some [USN:L6N45D0BT TEXT:"unusual manufacturing steps"], moving the production of his first sneaker models to China. ($1 = 0.8934 euros)

item.title: Ahead of the US midterms, Gen Z investors are making portfolio changes
item.description: Brandon Gaw is monitoring the news to adjust investments that he thinks could be hit hard by pre-election volatility ahead of the US midterms.
item.dc:creator: Hani Richter
item.content:encoded: Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor. Courtesy Brandon Gaw/Handout via REUTERS Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor, isn't just watching the news to stay in the know. He's also monitoring it to adjust investments that he thinks could be hit hard by pre-election volatility ahead of the US midterms . “When others are fearful, that's the best time to invest,” he says. One issue the 22-year-old is watching closely is the prospect of tighter restrictions involving Chinese-made memory chips entering the US market, as well as increased competition. Against this backdrop, Gaw says he is holding more cash and selling shares in smaller and newer companies that are more dependent on investors' excitement about AI, which he believes could be especially vulnerable to election uncertainty. Every few weeks, Gaw trades stocks worth $5,000 to $10,000. “In my opinion, those are going to get hit the most,” he says. Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor. Courtesy Brandon Gaw/Handout via REUTERS Gaw accepts he’s taking more risk because of his age compared to an investor who may need their money sooner for retirement or a house. But he’s also investing in more established companies, including Microsoft, Google, Nvidia and Apple. “If anything, I added a few more positions in those companies,” he says. “I don't think they're going to run out of business anytime soon.” For now, Gaw’s portfolio is fairly spread out: crypto, gold and silver collectively account for about 5% to 10%; ETFs make up around 30%; and individual stocks account for 60%. He has not made changes to his retirement investments. Taking a long-term view, Gaw says a market dip does not matter much to him if the S&P 500 falls. “I think these pullbacks are pretty good buying opportunities,” he says. THE WIDER TREND Nearly three-quarters of Gen Z investors have changed their retirement savings or portfolios in anticipation of the midterm election outcomes, compared to just 17% of Baby Boomers, according to a recent Nationwide Retirement Institute survey of over 2,000 US investors. Tyler McConville, a Wisconsin-based certified financial planner and private wealth advisor at Capital Group, says “The challenge is determining which information actually matters to a long-term financial plan.” While it is important to pay attention to elections and policy changes, markets have historically been influenced more by economic fundamentals and specific policy outcomes. “The biggest risk is when investors make long-term portfolio decisions based on short-term political concerns,” he says. KEY TAKEAWAYS Don’t make speculative trades. Use market-moving events as a reminder to review your investments and to consider how elections could affect certain sectors. Keep diversification in mind. Gaw spreads his investments across individual stocks, ETFs, crypto and precious metals, while reducing his exposure to stocks that he considers volatile. A diversified portfolio can help limit reliance on any one investment or sector. Focus on economic fundamentals. Rather than assuming one political party will be good or bad for stocks, consider factors such as inflation, interest rates, corporate earnings and specific policy changes when assessing your investments. Have a money lesson or story to share? Tell us what worked for you — or what didn’t — by emailing hani.richter@tr.com .

item.title: Top Democratic Virginia lawmaker charged by DOJ with running illegal cannabis operation
item.description: A senior Democratic state lawmaker in Virginia was charged with racketeering conspiracy, money laundering and other offenses for allegedly running an illegal cannabis business with members of her family, according to an indictment made public on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: A senior Democratic state lawmaker in Virginia was charged with racketeering conspiracy, money laundering and other offenses for allegedly running an illegal cannabis business with members of her family, according to an indictment made public on Thursday. Virginia State Senator L. Louise Lucas, 82, a long-serving Democrat, was charged along with two of her daughters, her grandson and three others, according to the indictment. Prosecutors allege that Lucas and her associates arranged for the distribution and sale of large amounts of marijuana. Recreational cannabis dispensaries are not yet legally authorized in the state. The indictment of a senior Democratic lawmaker comes less than two weeks before the November midterm elections , which will determine control of the US Congress, though Lucas and other members of the Virginia state Senate are not up for reelection this year. The Justice Department under President Donald Trump has repeatedly investigated and, in some cases, prosecuted prominent critics of the Republican president, and the department faced criticism for raiding Democratic US Representative [USN:L1N45Y0CB TEXT:"Ilhan Omar's home"] last week. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the investigation into Lucas has been ongoing for several years, rejecting suggestions that it was politically motivated. "The charges listed in the indictment reflect the alleged behavior of a public servant who put her own financial interests before the people she was elected to serve," Blanche said during a press conference. In a statement posted to social media, Lucas did not address the allegations in the indictment, but said the case resulted from her standing up to "people in power." "I will not intimidated. I will not be bullied. And I will not back down," Lucas wrote. Lucas surrendered to authorities on Thursday morning and was due to make her first court appearance later in the day in Norfolk, Virginia, federal court. Lucas serves as president pro tempore of the state Senate, meaning she leads the legislative body when the lieutenant governor is not present. She played a leading role in Virginia's unsuccessful attempt to redraw its legislative districts last year in a bid to keep pace with Republicans who were leading similar efforts in other states.

item.title: Peru taps fiscal strength to face El Niño impact, eases fiscal rules
item.description: Peru on Thursday unveiled a package of economic measures aimed at cushioning a potential slowdown from the El Niño weather phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Peru on Thursday unveiled a package of economic measures aimed at cushioning a potential slowdown from the El Niño weather phenomenon. Impacted firms will receive liquidity support and tax payment deferrals, Economy Minister Elmer Cuba said at a press conference, adding that Peru has the fiscal firepower to fund the measures. "Not all countries can do that - only solvent ones. The vast majority of the planet cannot respond like this," Cuba said Cuba cited three external shocks that could threaten Peru's economic momentum: El Niño, higher oil prices and rising global interest rates Peru's accumulated fiscal deficit in the 12 months through September stood at 0.9% of gross domestic product, the lowest level in four years, helped by stronger tax revenue, including income tax collections, according to preliminary central bank data Cuba also said Peru's economy could grow by more than the previously forecast 3.4%, even taking El Niño into account, though he did not give a revised estimate Scientist say that [USN:L6N43N0VE TEXT:"warmer ocean temperatures"] linked to the El Niño phenomenon are disrupting marine ecosystems off Peru's Pacific coast, threatening the country's fishing industry Speaking at the same press conference, President Keiko Fujimori said fiscal rules would be changed to allow an additional 18 billion soles ($5.22 billion) in investment next year Fujimori added that the change in fiscal rules contemplates raising the deficit to 2.4% of GDP in 2027, taking advantage of the public accounts' solidity, from the actual government's target of 1.8% for this year and 1.4% for 2027 ($1 = 3.4471 soles)

item.title: Perú anuncia política "contracíclica", con mayor déficit fiscal, para enfrentar a El Niño
item.description: Perú pondrá en marcha una política "contracíclica" elevando los topes de su meta de déficit fiscal para hacer mas inversiones y enfrentar choques externos en la economía local, como los efectos del fenómeno climático de El Niño, anunció el jueves el ministro de Economía del país sudamericano, Elmer Cuba.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino
item.content:encoded: Perú pondrá en marcha una política "contracíclica" elevando los topes de su meta de déficit fiscal para hacer mas inversiones y enfrentar choques externos en la economía local, como los efectos del fenómeno climático de El Niño, anunció el jueves el ministro de Economía del país sudamericano, Elmer Cuba. En una conferencia de prensa junto a la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, Cuba dijo que el Gobierno otorgará bonos a familias vulnerables, se inyectará liquidez y aplazarán pagos de impuestos a las empresas afectadas. El ministro dijo que el país minero tiene espacio fiscal para una respuesta frente a los choques externos, incluido el alza del petróleo y el aumento de las tasas de interés en el mundo. "Cada uno de estos choques amenaza el normal funcionamiento de cualquier economía y puede afectar el dinamismo de Perú, algo que no vamos a permitir porque tenemos espacio fiscal", manifestó Cuba. "No todos los países pueden hacer eso, solamente los países solventes", agregó. El déficit fiscal acumulado de Perú en los últimos 12 meses hasta septiembre fue del 0,9% del PIB, el más bajo en cuatro años, debido a mayores ingresos fiscales, según datos preliminares del banco central. Durante la conferencia de prensa, la presidenta Fujimori dijo que el Gobierno elevará los topes de la regla fiscal del 2027 para permitir la inversión de 18.000 millones de soles (unos 5.220 mil millones de dólares) más el próximo año. La mandataria detalló que, de ese monto, se destinarán 2.500 millones de soles en bonos para familias vulnerables, unos 2.000 millones de soles para el mantenimiento de la infraestructura y 13.000 millones de soles para culminar obras paralizadas. "La respuesta tiene que ser fuerte e histórica", afirmó. Fujimori dijo que el cambio de la regla fiscal contempla elevar el déficit a 2,4% del PBI en 2027, aprovechando la solidez de las cuentas públicas, desde la actual meta de un déficit fiscal de 1,8% este año y 1,4% el próximo. El Gobierno dijo recientemente que la temperatura del mar en Perú ha llegado a sus niveles máximos en esta época del año, lo que hace prever que enfrentará el fenómeno climático de El Niño [USN:L1N4620VD TEXT:"más poderoso"] de las últimas décadas. "Será un Niño sin precedente en los últimos 70 años", dijo Cuba, quien, sin embargo, agregó que la economía del país podría crecer este año más del 3,4% que espera el gobierno, aunque no proporcionó una nueva cifra. El Niño ya está afectando a la industria de la pesca, a la agricultura y está presionando los precios. Por otra parte, se prevé que lluvias e inundaciones dañen infraestructura como carreteras y servicios básicos. A mediados de septiembre, el Banco Central de Perú [USN:L1N45A0RI TEXT:"redujo su proyección de crecimiento"] para la economía del país minero a un 3,2% en 2026, desde el 3,4% que había previsto, debido a los efectos de El Niño. (1 dólar = 3,45 soles)

item.title: CSN, Vale, Braskem e outras indústrias compram gás em leilão inédito da PPSA
item.description: A siderúrgica CSN , a mineradora Vale e a petroquímica Braskem , entre outras grandes companhias industriais, venceram lotes de gás natural da União ofertados em leilão inédito do insumo realizado pela Pré-Sal Petróleo (PPSA) nesta quinta-feira, segundo dados da plataforma do certame.
item.dc:creator: Leticia Augusto
item.content:encoded: A siderúrgica CSN (CSNA3.SA) , a mineradora Vale (VALE3.SA) e a petroquímica Braskem (BRKM3.SA) , entre outras grandes companhias industriais, venceram lotes de gás natural da União ofertados em leilão inédito do insumo realizado pela Pré-Sal Petróleo (PPSA) nesta quinta-feira, segundo dados da plataforma do certame. O primeiro leilão para venda direta de gás à indústria brasileira terminou com todo o volume oferecido, de 1,1 milhão m³/dia dividido em 110 lotes, arrematado por 23 empresas de cinco setores grandes consumidores de gás. O preço médio do gás negociado ficou em US$5,83/MMBtu, o que, segundo uma autoridade do Ministério de Minas e Energia, proporcionará às indústrias participantes reduções de 38% a 57% frente à média de US$12/MMBtu usada como referência de mercado. No setor químico e petroquímico, que contou com o maior volume de gás disponibilizado, de 350 mil m³/dia, foram vencedoras a Braskem (BRKM3.SA) , Rhodia, Evonik, Ingredion e Peróxidos do Brasil. Entre as siderúrgicas, metalúrgicas e mineradoras, com 320 mil m³/dia de gás ofertado, foram vencedoras CSN, Gerdau Aços Longos, Samarco, Ternium Brasil e Vale. Também contrataram gás a Yara Fertilizantes e Multitécnica Industrial, do setor de fertilizantes nitrogenados, com 130 mil m³/dia, e outras 11 empresas dos setores ceramista (200 mil m³/dia) e vidreiro (100 mil m³/dia). Em relação a preços, os menores lances foram de US$4,00/MMBtu para o setor vidreiro, US$1,86/MMBtu para o ceramista, US$2,30/MMBtu para o siderúrgico, metalúrgico e de mineração, US$1,92/MMBtu para químico e petroquímico e US$1,82/MMBtu para fertilizantes nitrogenados. Os lances tiveram uma referência inicial de US$1,80/MMBtu para todas as disputas. Com fornecimento entre março e dezembro de 2027, o gás vendido neste leilão será entregue no Complexo de Energias Boaventura da Petrobras, o antigo Comperj, em Itaboraí (RJ). A partir dali, cada comprador contrata o transporte por gasodutos até suas fábricas. DEMANDA REPRIMIDA O leilão da PPSA é o primeiro de venda direta a consumidores do gás natural pertencente à União. A iniciativa buscou ampliar o número de agentes no mercado de gás e contribuir para a competitividade da indústria brasileira. "O que o dia de hoje comprovou foi que a demanda (por gás) não só existe, mas você tem setores industriais ávidos por adquirir o gás natural a um preço competitivo, com uma formação de preço em leilão", disse Renato Dutra, secretário de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis do Ministério de Minas e Energia. Segundo ele, as reduções de dois dígitos de preço mostram que é possível fazer política pública com o gás da União, ajudando na competitividade da indústria nacional, "com um preço justo e adequado no sentido de remunerar as infraestruturas (de escoamento e processamento de gás)". Segundo o presidente da PPSA, Luis Fernando Paroli, o Brasil terá um [USN:L1N4680YA TEXT:"novo leilão"] de gás natural da União à indústria em 2027, com oferta de 1,8 milhão de metros cúbicos por dia.

item.title: Líder da oposição do Equador González é presa por supostas irregularidades em financiamento de campanha
item.description: Uma proeminente política de esquerda do Equador, que ficou em segundo lugar nas duas últimas eleições, atrás do presidente Daniel Noboa, foi presa, informou nesta quinta-feira a chefe de seu partido.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Valencia
item.content:encoded: Uma proeminente política de esquerda do Equador, que ficou em segundo lugar nas duas últimas eleições, atrás do presidente Daniel Noboa, foi presa, informou nesta quinta-feira a chefe de seu partido. Luisa González, protegida do ex-presidente socialista Rafael Correa, está sendo investigada por supostas irregularidades no financiamento político e nos gastos de campanha nas eleições de 2023. Em uma postagem no X, González disse que a acusação era “absurda” e pediu união aos membros de seu partido para alcançar a liberdade e a democracia no Equador. A líder do partido Revolução Cidadã, Gabriela Rivadeneira, confirmou a prisão em uma postagem nas redes sociais e argumentou que ela teve motivação política. “Exigimos a libertação imediata de Luisa González, que não deveria ter que enfrentar um processo de perseguição e tortura imposto por este governo”, disse ela aos repórteres. Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, a Procuradoria-Geral informou que a investigação buscava esclarecer a origem dos recursos utilizados para financiar a propaganda eleitoral entre maio e agosto de 2023. “Uma rede de pessoas jurídicas foi utilizada para canalizar aproximadamente US$500.000 para contratar e adquirir publicidade de campanha. Os recursos teriam sido canalizados sem a divulgação de sua origem ou da identidade dos contribuintes”, afirmou o vídeo. Rivadeneira afirmou que os recursos da campanha de 2023 foram totalmente contabilizados e que as multas financeiras impostas anteriormente pela autoridade eleitoral já haviam sido pagas, reiterando declarações anteriores de González. O ex-presidente Correa, que apoiou a candidatura de González, também contestou as alegações. “Não se trata de legalidade, nem de se as regras estão sendo seguidas ou não. Trata-se de uma perseguição brutal e simples”, disse ele em um programa de rádio local. A Procuradoria-Geral do Equador, em uma postagem nas redes sociais, informou que sete pessoas estão sob investigação por “inconsistências nas contribuições e na origem lícita dos recursos” durante a campanha presidencial de 2023. Três pessoas foram presas até o momento e responderão a acusações por suposta lavagem de dinheiro, informou o órgão, sem revelar seus nomes completos. González perdeu as eleições de 2023 e 2025 para Noboa e alegou fraude na derrota do ano passado. Ela tentou concorrer às eleições locais marcadas para 29 de novembro, mas não conseguiu registrar sua candidatura devido às regras de registro dos partidos.

item.title: Detienen a excandidata ecuatoriana Luisa González por acusación sobre fondos electorales
item.description: La dirigencia del partido izquierdista ecuatoriano Revolución Ciudadana informó sobre la detención en la madrugada del jueves de Luisa González, principal rival del presidente Daniel Noboa en las dos últimas elecciones, que calificó la acusación de "abusrda".
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Valencia
item.content:encoded: La dirigencia del partido izquierdista ecuatoriano Revolución Ciudadana informó sobre la detención en la madrugada del jueves de Luisa González, principal rival del presidente Daniel Noboa en las dos últimas elecciones, que calificó la acusación de "abusrda". González, una protegida del expresidente socialista Rafael Correa, es investigada, juntos a otros miembros de su partido, por presuntas irregularidades en la financiación política y los gastos de campaña del 2023. "Hoy me toca a mi ser detenida por una acusación absurda", escribió González en una carta publicado en su cuenta de X. "Los presos políticos de la dictadura están siendo maltratados y torturados". "Hemos llegado a una situación insostenible", añadió. La presidenta del partido Revolución Ciudadana, Gabriela Rivadeneira, dijo a periodistas que los fondos de la campaña de 2023 fueron debidamente justificados y que las sanciones económicas impuestas antes por la autoridad electoral ya habían sido pagadas, reiterando así declaraciones previas de la propia González. El movimiento político exigió la inmediata libertad de González ante la falta de pruebas en su contra. Correa, quien respaldó la candidatura de González, también rechazó las acusaciones. “Aquí no se trata de legalidad (...) es brutal y simple persecución y frente a eso sólo queda resistir de todas formas posibles", dijo a Radio Pichincha. "A Luisa la van a enterrar en vida". La Fiscalía General del Estado informó de que siete personas están siendo investigadas en relación con este caso —tres de ellas detenidas, de quienes solo se proporcionaron sus iniciales— y añadió que en las próximas horas presentará cargos por presunto lavado de activos. Más tarde, la institución explicó que además de los fondos declarados ante la autoridad electoral, se habrían utilizado "un entramado" de personas jurídicas para canalizar aproximadamente 500.000 dólares para la campaña electoral, de acuerdo a lo recabado en la investigación. "Los fondos se habrían canalizado sin trasparentar su procedencia ni la identidad de quienes habrían aportado”, añadió la fiscalía en un video publicado en redes sociales. González perdió frente a Noboa tanto en las elecciones de 2023 como en las de 2025. Tras la derrota del año pasado, denunció un supuesto fraude. Intentó postularse en los comicios seccionales del 29 de noviembre, pero no pudo inscribirse por las normas de registro de partidos políticos.

item.title: Ecuadorean opposition leader Gonzalez arrested over alleged irregularities in campaign financing
item.description: A prominent leftist politician in Ecuador who was runner-up to President Daniel Noboa in the last two elections has been arrested, the head of her party said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Valencia
item.content:encoded: A prominent leftist politician in Ecuador who was runner-up to President Daniel Noboa in the last two elections has been arrested, the head of her party said on Thursday. Luisa Gonzalez, a protege of former socialist President Rafael Correa, is under investigation over alleged irregularities in political financing and campaign spending in the 2023 election. In a post on X, Gonzalez said the accusation was "absurd" and she asked for unity from members of her party to reach freedom and democracy in Ecuador. The head of the Citizens' Revolution party, Gabriela Rivadeneira, confirmed the arrest in a social media post and argued it was politically motivated. "We demand the immediate release of Luisa Gonzalez, who should not have to face a process of persecution and torture imposed by this government," she told reporters. In a video posted on social media, the Attorney General's Office said the investigation was seeking to clarify the source of the funds used to finance election advertising between May and August 2023. "A network of legal entities was used to channel approximately $500,000 to contract and purchase campaign advertising. The funds were allegedly channelled without disclosing their source or the identity of those who contributed them,” it said in a video. Rivadeneira said the 2023 campaign funds were fully accounted for and prior financial penalties imposed by the electoral authority had been paid, echoing earlier statements from Gonzalez. Former President Correa, who backed Gonzalez's candidacy, also disputed the allegations. "This is not about legality, or whether the rules are being followed or not. It is brutal and simple persecution," he told a local radio program. The Ecuadorean Attorney General's Office in a social media post said seven people are under investigation over "inconsistencies in the contributions and the lawful source of the funds" during the 2023 presidential campaign. Three people so far have been arrested and will face charges for alleged money laundering, it said, without providing their full names. Gonzalez lost both the 2023 and 2025 elections to Noboa, and alleged fraud in last year's loss. She had attempted to run in local elections set for November 29 but was unable to register her candidacy due to party registration rules.

item.title: UDPATE 1 Cricket-England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase
item.description: England's Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England's Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare on Thursday. The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India's Shubman Gill. In the process, Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes. Brook's scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England's innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage. He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd. The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. "Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn't matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn't even count," Brook said. "Heart-breaking. I think you've hit the nail on the head there. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430, but that's life, that's cricket," he added. "You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they've just played an absolute blinder there ... "We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We've got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore." Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls as England piled up 429-4. But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries. Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook's record-breaking innings all in vain. Tongue was England's most successful bowler with 3-79. England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi on Tuesday to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.

item.title: Ebola patient in Nigeria believed to have contracted disease in Uganda, Switzerland says
item.description: The Ebola patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, is believed to have contracted the disease while travelling in Uganda, a Swiss government statement to Reuters said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Clement Bonnerot, Anait Miridzhanian, Robbie Corey-Boulet
item.content:encoded: The Ebola patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, is believed to have contracted the disease while travelling in Uganda, a Swiss government statement to Reuters said on Thursday. Nigeria reported the case, its first Ebola case in more than a decade, on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that was announced in Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-May and has since become the [USN:L6N4421DF TEXT:"fastest-spreading"] on record. Ugandan authorities have said the woman who fell ill in Nigeria had travelled to eastern Congo before transiting through Uganda. But the World Health Organization and Africa's top health agency said on Thursday they had not received confirmed information that the woman had travelled to Congo. The woman "has been in a private clinic in Abuja for around a week with symptoms. She is believed to have contracted the virus whilst travelling to Uganda around two weeks ago," said an emailed statement from the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs. "Her husband is in isolation; he has not shown any symptoms. He was travelling with his wife when she is believed to have contracted Ebola." Uganda reported 20 cases in May and June, mostly imported from Congo, but the World Health Organization declared the country [USN:L6N44N0V1 TEXT:"Ebola-free"] in August. Ugandan government spokesperson Alan Kasujja told Reuters late on Thursday that Uganda had no Ebola cases. "That's a fact. If we did, as has happened before, we'd be the first to say," he said. Asked whether the Ugandan government had proof that the woman had travelled to Congo, Kasujja said, "Like what? A passport stamp? Without infringing on the patient’s rights?" AFRICA CDC, WHO SAY NO INFORMATION THAT PATIENT WENT TO CONGO Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention official Wessam Mankoula said on Thursday that Nigeria and Uganda were sharing information to establish the patient's movements and possible source of exposure. "So far, there is no validated information (that) this case traveled to DRC (Democratic Republic of Congo)," Mankoula told an online press conference. The WHO said information it had received about the case did not include travel outside Uganda. "The facts which we have received is that the patient returned to Abuja on October 3, being away from September 16 in Uganda," WHO representative to Nigeria Pavel Ursu told the press conference. Ursu said the focus in Nigeria was now on containing the viral infection and that the patient remained hospitalised, with her biochemical markers improving. Jean Kaseya, Africa CDC director, told Reuters on Wednesday that the patient had been on a two-week holiday in Uganda. Patrick Otim, a WHO emergency response manager, said on Thursday the source of her infection was still unknown as health authorities were working to piece together her travel history. One issue under investigation is which health facilities the woman visited in Abuja after the onset of her symptoms and before her hospitalisation 48 hours later, Otim said. KENYA TRACES ALL CONTACTS OF FIRST CASE Separately, a senior Kenyan health official said authorities there had now traced all 135 contacts of the country's first Ebola case, which was [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"confirmed on October 6"] and after which a further eight cases have been reported. "We have been able to account for them 100%," health ministry director-general Patrick Amoth said. He said the last contact to be traced was a Ugandan citizen who had arrived in Kenya in early October on the same flight as the index patient but exited by road via the Namanga border post with Tanzania, which meant it took more time to find him. Africa CDC is investigating whether the Kenyan case may have come into contact with the patient being treated in Nigeria, as both travelled from Uganda's Entebbe airport on the same day, Mankoula said. Transmission between the two was one of the possible scenarios being examined, he said. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, whether living or dead. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. The rare Ebola species behind the current outbreak kills about half of those infected and has no approved treatment or vaccine. So far the outbreak is confirmed to have killed about 4,700 people across the four African countries that have reported cases, according to the Africa CDC.

item.title: Yen se dispara por preocupación por el petróleo, la IA y Francia
item.description: El yen registró el jueves su mayor subida diaria en casi un mes, porque los inversionistas lo buscaron como refugio ante la inestabilidad de los mercados bursátiles, los altos precios del crudo por la guerra en Oriente Medio y las dudas sobre la rentabilidad futura de la inteligencia artificial (IA).
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El yen registró el jueves su mayor subida diaria en casi un mes, porque los inversionistas lo buscaron como refugio ante la inestabilidad de los mercados bursátiles, los altos precios del crudo por la guerra en Oriente Medio y las dudas sobre la rentabilidad futura de la inteligencia artificial (IA). En tanto, el dólar se apreciaba frente al euro, porque la preocupación por los disturbios sociales en Francia y el deterioro de las perspectivas fiscales del país pesaban más que las inquietudes sobre el sector de la IA, que provocaba una caída de las acciones estadounidenses. "La IA está poniendo nerviosa a la gente, al igual que el petróleo (...) y Francia. Es evidente que hay un ligero grado de aversión al riesgo en el mercado", dijo Chris Scicluna, de Daiwa Capital Markets. Los precios del petróleo subieron alrededor de un 3%, a un máximo en cinco meses, después de que nuevos ataques hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaron el temor a una escalada del conflicto en Oriente Medio y a nuevas interrupciones en el suministro. El yen japonés se apreció un 0,75%, a 156,96 unidades por dólar. Parte de la evolución del yen también podría deberse a que se está acercando al nivel clave de 160 unidades por dólar, lo que se considera que aumenta la probabilidad de una nueva intervención de las autoridades japonesas para apuntalar la moneda. El dólar se debilitó un 0,42% frente al franco suizo, otro refugio tradicional, que cotizaba en 0,821 unidades por dólar. El índice dólar , que mide la cotización de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas que incluye al yen y al euro, cayó un 0,08%, a 101,6 unidades, mientras que el euro bajaba un 0,09%, a 1,1222 dólares. La preocupación sobre la capacidad de Francia para gestionar su enorme deuda ha perjudicado a los bonos del Estado francés y ha avivado el temor por otros países muy endeudados de la zona del euro. El diferencial entre los rendimientos de los bonos a 10 años de Francia y Alemania alcanzó los 177,7 puntos básicos el jueves, la mayor diferencia desde 2011.

item.title: Israeli fire kills four people in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in the Gaza Strip in separate incidents on Thursday, health officials in the enclave said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in the Gaza Strip in separate incidents on Thursday, health officials in the enclave said. In Gaza City, a strike on a car killed at least one person, medics said. They earlier said there had been two deaths. A crowd gathered around the burning wreckage, as orange-vested emergency crews sprayed it with water, photos from the scene showed. Other strikes killed a Palestinian man on a bike in the southern city of Khan Younis and a man near Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, and gunfire killed a woman near the Jabalia refugee camp, in the north, the medics added. Israel's military said it had struck Hamas militants in Khan Younis, Nuseirat and Gaza City, but that it was not aware of the reported incident in Jabalia. The Hamas-led Interior Ministry in Gaza said an Israeli airstrike killed a non-commissioned officer and wounded another officer from the drug control police department after hitting their vehicle while returning from an assignment in Tel al-Hawa neighborhood. Israel, which says the Hamas militant group has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of [USN:L6N45Q023 TEXT:"a year-old ceasefire"], has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal. Last year's US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. Israeli airstrikes have continued. At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

item.title: Barril toca máximos de cinco meses ya que ataques de hutíes generan temores por suministro
item.description: Los precios del petróleo subían el jueves alrededor de un 3%, a un máximo de cinco meses, luego de que ataques de los hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaron la preocupación por posibles nuevas interrupciones en el suministro de energía.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subían el jueves alrededor de un 3%, a un máximo de cinco meses, luego de que ataques de los hutíes en Arabia Saudita avivaron la preocupación por posibles nuevas interrupciones en el suministro de energía. * Los futuros del crudo Brent trepaban 3,51 dólares, o un 3,2%, a 112,33 dólares por barril, a las 1705 GMT, mientras que el crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate (WTI) sumaba 2,14 dólares, o un 2,2%, a 99,29 dólares. * Esto llevó al Brent a entrar en terreno de sobrecompra técnica por tercera vez en una semana, situando al contrato en camino a su cierre más alto desde el 4 de mayo. * Saudi Aramco ordenó al personal evacuar su sede en Dhahran, en el golfo Pérsico, cerca de Baréin, reportó Reuters, a medida que se intensificaban los combates entre el mayor exportador de crudo del mundo y los hutíes de Yemen. * Los enfrentamientos entre los hutíes y una coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita, que respalda al gobierno de Yemen reconocido internacionalmente, se han recrudecido desde que el grupo alineado con Irán avanzó hacia el estrecho de Mandeb, un punto crítico para la navegación situado en la entrada del mar Rojo. * "Los informes que indican que las exportaciones de crudo de Oriente Medio superan los niveles previos al conflicto quedan más que compensados por los ataques a buques en el estrecho de Ormuz y las ofensivas hutíes contra Arabia Saudita y su infraestructura petrolera", dijo Tamas Varga, analista de PVM Oil. * Los analistas de Morgan Stanley estimaron en una nota que las exportaciones de crudo de Oriente Medio rondaron los 17 millones de barriles por día la semana pasada. Según datos de Kpler, en los 12 meses anteriores al inicio del conflicto, las exportaciones de crudo de la región promediaron cerca de 18 millones de barriles diarios. * En Estados Unidos, la refinería Valero Energy registró el mayor beneficio trimestral de su historia, superando las expectativas de Wall Street, ya que las interrupciones derivadas del conflicto en Oriente Medio provocaron un fuerte aumento en los márgenes de refinado durante el tercer trimestre.

item.title: India overcome New Zealand fightback to win T20 opener
item.description: India overcame a spirited New Zealand fightback after a blazing start to secure a thrilling four-wicket victory in Christchurch on Thursday and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match T20 series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India overcame a spirited New Zealand fightback after a blazing start to secure a thrilling four-wicket victory in Christchurch on Thursday and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match T20 series. India survived a mid-innings wobble in a 226-run chase after openers Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma laid the platform, with Shreyas Iyer's contribution reviving the chase and Naman Dhir applying the finishing touches to seal victory in 19.4 overs. "When they (openers) click, they set up the game for us and the rest of us try to steady the ship and finish," India captain Iyer said. "He (Dhir) gives us lots of options. I personally feel the calm and composed nature he showed tonight, it was magnificent." Put in to bat, New Zealand made the most of favourable conditions as openers Tim Seifert and Finn Allen set the tone before Glenn Phillips produced a dazzling knock to propel the hosts to 225-4. The total was New Zealand's biggest T20 score against India on home soil, but the visitors completed their highest-ever successful run chase despite a stuttering middle phase. Samson and Abhishek stitched together a 93-run opening stand, with Samson hammering 67 off 33 balls, including eight fours and four sixes, as India surged to 94-1 in the powerplay. New Zealand hit back by removing three batters in quick succession, but Iyer countered with 42 off 28 balls to wrest back the momentum, before a late flourish from Dhir (42 not out)took India over the line. "They (India openers) put us under pressure. Another big powerplay from them. We were not at our best," New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said. "In the middle, we did well to squeeze them. Tight game and both teams might look at things that could have gone here or there." Seifert and Allen had earlier given New Zealand a solid platform, helping the hosts reach 65-1 in the powerplay, with Allen blasting 45 off 24 balls. Phillips then took charge, producing an unbeaten 82 off 40 deliveries, including eight fours and three sixes, while Bevon Jacobs added 31 before being run out. India's bowlers struggled to contain the scoring, with all five used going at 10 runs an over or more. Bhuvneshwar Kumar, playing his first T20 international in four years after last featuring against New Zealand in 2022, endured an expensive return with figures of 0-49. The second T20 will be played on Saturday in Christchurch.

item.title: Rifts emerge in Libya as eastern parliament backs central bank chief's resignation
item.description: A new contest for control of the central bank in divided Libya could emerge after the eastern-based parliament said on Thursday it approved in principle the resignation of its governor, Naji Issa, and backed a member of the bank's board to replace him on an interim basis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A new contest for control of the central bank in divided Libya could emerge after the eastern-based parliament said on Thursday it approved in principle the resignation of its governor, Naji Issa, and backed a member of the bank's board to replace him on an interim basis. The House of Representatives's (HoR) spokesperson said parliament backed Fowzi Musbah Abukhzam, the board member, to temporarily fill the role at the central bank. In the western half of the North African country, however, Naji Mukhtar Ali, the first deputy of the High Council of State (HCS), rejected Issa's resignation and told him to stay in his post. Yet the head of HCS, Mohamed Takala, contradicted his first deputy's position, and called on Abukhzam to carry on his duties on an interim basis, in line with the HoR decision, underlining some rifts even among the main Libyan factions. "You are requested to assume your duties and carry out the functions of the Governor of the Central Bank of Libya on an interim basis, pending an agreement with the House of Representatives on the appointment of a Governor for the Central Bank," Takala said in a letter to Abukhzam, which was viewed by Reuters and confirmed by a person at the HCS. The eastern parliament will discuss Issa's resignation in a coming session, its spokesperson wrote on X. In August, Issa submitted his resignation to the two legislative chambers, saying he could not continue in his post but without explaining why, according to two documents seen by Reuters at the time. DIVIDED COUNTRY Libya has been split since 2014 into rival authorities in the west and east that emerged from the turmoil following the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011. It is now run by the eastern-based HoR, which was elected in 2014, and the western-based HCS, whose members were drawn from a parliament elected in 2012. After Issa submitted his resignation, both chambers had said he should stay in the position until the issue was discussed. In reaction to Thursday's decision by the eastern parliament, Ali, the HCS first deputy in the west, rejected what he called "the unilateral measures taken by the presidency of the House of Representatives." "You are requested to continue performing your tasks," Ali told Issa in a letter seen by Reuters that was confirmed by a central bank official and an HCS source. Issa took up the post in 2024 when the two legislative chambers agreed on his appointment as a way to end a stand off over control of the central bank. Separately, the central bank said in a statement on its verified Facebook page that it condemned the forced entry of people into its headquarters, violating the governor’s office in his absence. It did not explain the incident, but it said it holds all those involved responsible for any consequences, "foremost among them the Ministry of Defence, given its responsibility for protecting and securing the bank’s headquarters." In a separate incident, masked men tried to [USN:L1N4670MR TEXT:"storm the country's financial oversight agency"] on Wednesday, in what Libya's UN mission called an "unacceptable" attempt to install a senior employee by force.

item.title: France's Macron tightens curbs on protests, blaming hard left for unrest
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"riots and looting"]. Speaking after a meeting with intelligence chiefs and senior ministers, [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"Macron"] said demonstrations organised by groups such as trade unions would be allowed to go ahead but could be diverted along alternative routes to protect businesses. "Last Saturday we had political and seditious acts by ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic," he said. His comments came as authorities across France prepared for fresh protests following some of the country's [USN:L1N4670D4 TEXT:"worst urban unrest in years"]. Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said he wanted voting rights suspended for people who defy bans on taking part in demonstrations, and restrictions on social media access for people involved in violence, looting or attacks on police. All protests planned for Saturday in Marseille and Lyon, France's second- and third-largest cities, have been banned, local authorities said. Yet [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"fresh demonstrations"] are already taking shape before what officials fear could be another volatile weekend. France's main student union, UNEF, has called for rallies on Saturday, while the Yellow Vest movement, the anti-establishment force that emerged in 2018, has filed plans for a march through central Paris. Businesses in central Paris have begun boarding up their shop windows in case of violence. Luxury goods group Hermes said [USN:S8N3Z600A TEXT:"it had stepped up security measures"] at its French stores. Organisers of the Art Basel Paris international art collectors fair being held in a central Paris exhibition hall said it would be closed all weekend. Elsewhere, authorities in the northern city of Orleans were bracing for potential unrest as the far-right National Rally was due to hold an annual meeting and unions and left-wing groups planned demonstrations. A student protest called for Thursday in Paris was initially banned but eventually allowed to go ahead, though metro stations in central Paris were nonetheless shuttered by transit authorities in anticipation of unauthorised gatherings. PUBLIC ANGER France was rocked on October 17 by violence on the fringes of nationwide protests, exposing the depth of public anger and raising questions about the security services' ability to keep order. Two people have been arrested over an arson attack on Limoges city hall, French officials and media said. A third consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas affected by the violence, offering the government some respite ahead of the weekend. The unrest has laid bare a deeper malaise in France, where soaring energy costs, pressure on household budgets and concerns over deteriorating public services have fuelled growing frustration among workers and younger people. The French political class has also descended into a bitter blame game, with the government accusing [USN:L6N4670XJ TEXT:"far-left"] political groups of stoking the unrest. Highlighting investor unease, the [USN:L6N46814J TEXT:"risk premium"] on French government debt over safe-haven German bonds widened to its highest in 15 years on Thursday, while France's benchmark 10-year bond yield hit 5.14%, its highest level since July 2002.

item.title: França relata primeiro caso humano do vírus Shamonda após morte de paciente
item.description: A França relatou nesta quinta-feira o primeiro caso humano do vírus Shamonda, normalmente encontrado em animais de criação, em um paciente que morreu no hospital, embora autoridades tenham afirmado que não há risco para a população em geral.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide, Gus Trompiz
item.content:encoded: A França relatou nesta quinta-feira o primeiro caso humano do vírus Shamonda, normalmente encontrado em animais de criação, em um paciente que morreu no hospital, embora autoridades tenham afirmado que não há risco para a população em geral. O homem estava hospitalizado em Lyon devido a uma doença grave não relacionada, informou um representante do Ministério da Saúde da França a jornalistas. A vítima tinha cerca de 60 anos e morava na região de Lyon, noticiou o jornal local Le Progrès. A Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) informou que está em contato com as autoridades francesas a respeito do assunto. "Com base nas informações atuais e no conhecimento sobre a transmissão de vírus intimamente relacionados, trata-se de um caso humano isolado; é improvável que isso leve a uma propagação mais ampla neste momento", afirmou a OMS, sediada em Genebra, que coordena respostas a questões e emergências de saúde pública em nível internacional. "Estamos, claramente, diante de um caso sem precedentes do ponto de vista científico e virológico. Ele está associado ao sistema imunológico severamente debilitado desse homem", explicou Gregory Emery, diretor-geral de saúde da França, a jornalistas. "Do ponto de vista médico e de saúde pública, não há motivo para alerta nem crise", acrescentou. VÍRUS EM ANIMAIS NA EUROPA Transmitido por mosquitos picadores e mais comumente encontrado em bovinos, o vírus Shamonda também já foi detectado em cavalos, alpacas, ovelhas e cabras, informou a Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal (WOAH, na sigla em inglês). Não há relato de transmissão de gado para humanos ou de humano para humano, disse Emery. Atualmente, não há vacinas comercialmente disponíveis contra o vírus Shamonda, informou a WOAH. Identificado na Nigéria em meados da década de 1960, o vírus Shamonda foi confirmado pela primeira vez na Europa no final de julho, após testes genômicos em bovinos doentes no sul da Alemanha, na Suíça e no leste da França. Um relatório do boletim semanal de vigilância sanitária animal da França indicou que o vírus também havia sido detectado na Áustria, Bélgica, Irlanda, Itália, Liechtenstein, Luxemburgo, Holanda, Portugal, Eslovênia, Espanha e na ilha de Jersey, no Reino Unido. O vírus provoca diversos efeitos nos animais. O gado infectado apresenta diarreia, fraqueza, perda de apetite e, com menos frequência, febre, informaram as autoridades francesas de saúde animal. Um estudo realizado em nove fazendas leiteiras francesas constatou que a produção de leite caiu em até 75% nos rebanhos afetados.

item.title: El oro cae a mínimo de más de dos meses por el temor a la inflación
item.description: El oro cayó el jueves a un mínimo de más de dos meses, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo avivó el temor a la inflación, lo que reforzó las expectativas de que las tasas de interés podrían mantenerse altas durante más tiempo, mientras los inversores esperaban con interés la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel John, Anushree Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: El oro cayó el jueves a un mínimo de más de dos meses, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo avivó el temor a la inflación, lo que reforzó las expectativas de que las tasas de interés podrían mantenerse altas durante más tiempo, mientras los inversores esperaban con interés la reunión de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana. El oro al contado cayó un 2,4%, a 4.041,39 dólares por onza, a las 1805 GMT, su nivel más bajo desde el 3 de agosto. Los futuros del oro estadounidense para entrega en diciembre cerraron con un descenso del 2,2%, a 4.060,40 dólares por onza. Los precios del petróleo subían alrededor de un 3%, a máximos de cinco meses, después de que los ataques hutíes en Arabia Saudita hicieron crecer el temor a nuevas interrupciones del suministro energético. "Hemos visto cómo los precios de la energía subían de la noche a la mañana. Y, como consecuencia de ello, está aumentando la preocupación por las presiones inflacionistas. A medida que aumentan esas presiones inflacionistas, vemos el resultado obvio de los temores de que la Fed vaya a seguir subiendo las tasas de interés", dijo David Meger, director de operaciones con metales de High Ridge Futures. Aunque el oro suele considerarse una cobertura frente a la inflación, el aumento de las tasas de interés reduce el atractivo de este activo, que no rinde intereses. Los datos de la semana pasada sobre la inflación de los consumidores y de los productores en Estados Unidos fueron más altos de lo esperado, en gran parte debido a que los costos energéticos siguen subiendo. Esto refuerza los argumentos a favor de una política monetaria más restrictiva, aunque se sigue esperando que los responsables de la Fed mantengan el "statu quo" cuando se reúnan los días 27 y 28 de octubre. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores descuentan una probabilidad del 91% de que se produzca una subida en diciembre. Los datos sobre el gasto en consumo personal (PCE) de Estados Unidos, cuya publicación está prevista para el 29 de octubre y que el banco central sigue muy de cerca, podrían ofrecer más pistas sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés. Entre otros metales, la plata al contado cayó un 5,4%, a 54,84 dólares por onza; el platino bajó un 3,7%, a 1.570,85 dólares, mientras que el paladio descendió un 2,7%, a 1.057,83 dólares.

item.title: US refiner Valero posts record quarterly profit as supply disruptions boost margins
item.description: Refiner Valero Energy kicked off earnings season for US refiners on Thursday by posting its highest-ever quarterly profit, beating Wall Street expectations, as fuel supply disruptions due to wars in Iran and Ukraine boosted margins during the third quarter.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao, Vallari Srivastava
item.content:encoded: Refiner Valero Energy (VLO.N) kicked off earnings season for US refiners on Thursday by posting its highest-ever quarterly profit, beating Wall Street expectations, as fuel supply disruptions due to wars in Iran and Ukraine boosted margins during the third quarter. Diesel, used in manufacturing and agriculture, has hit record high prices, and gasoline prices are also elevated, creating pain for consumers and US President Donald Trump's Republican Party ahead of next month's midterm elections, but enriching refiners. The 3-2-1 crack spread , which measures US refinery margins, gained more than 150% during the July-September period, from a year earlier. Valero said its refining margin per barrel of throughput nearly tripled to $39.24 in the quarter, with adjusted operating earnings in the refining segment jumping over 400% to $8.8 billion from a year earlier. Valero shares were down 3%. NO SIGNS OF SOFTENING DEMAND The US, the world's largest crude oil producer and second-largest refiner after China, ramped up exports of crude, gasoline, diesel and jet fuel to record levels earlier this year, following war-driven supply disruptions. "Export demand for diesel is also very, very strong, both to Latin America and Europe," Chief Operating Officer Gary Simmons said during a call with investors. He said economic and trucking industry indicators show demand for the fuel will remain robust. US refiners are also running at 95% to 100% of capacity, with many delaying planned maintenance to benefit from high energy prices. Valero plans to operate its refineries in the United States and Britain at 96% to 99% of their combined total throughput capacity of 3 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter. Valero said it has completed an optimization project at its St. Charles refinery in Louisiana, increasing production capacity of alkylate and gasoline. The Texas-based company posted adjusted profit of $23.90 per share, up about 553% from the same time last year. "While the volatility is probably not behind us at this point, we're in a good position to be even more aggressive with shareholder returns," Chief Financial Officer Homer Bhullar said. "Whether margins and cash flow profile of our business remain strong or not, our long-term targets on cash have really not changed."

item.title: Lockheed lands Pentagon deal for 850 F-35 jets, lifts annual forecast
item.description: Lockheed Martin announced an agreement on Thursday to sell the Pentagon at least 850 stealthy F-35 Lightning II fighter jets over the next 10 years, a deal worth at least $78 billion.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone, Aatreyee Dasgupta
item.content:encoded: Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) announced an agreement on Thursday to sell the Pentagon at least 850 stealthy F-35 Lightning II fighter jets over the next 10 years, a deal worth at least $78 billion. Lockheed shares surged as much as 10%, on track for their biggest percentage gain in three months. The US defense contractor raised its annual sales and profit forecasts to beat Wall Street estimates, as geopolitical conflicts drove demand for its systems. The fighter jet, which the company considers the world's most advanced, uses stealth technology to evade enemy detection. It is at the core of Lockheed's aeronautics division, which generates nearly 40% of the company's quarterly revenue. Under the agreement, Lockheed will aim to maintain annual production at 156 aircraft for US and international customers, and the company will self-fund at least $7 billion in initiatives that support the F-35 program. "That investment will help both with the ability to produce the capabilities on the production line now, as well as in the supply base, the tooling, and the workforce repair lines," OJ Sanchez, president of Lockheed Martin's aeronautics segment, told Reuters. As the fleet of F-35 jets grows, repair and maintenance needs have increased, straining the industry's F-35 production and repair capacity. Part of the investment will fund new repair lines at the original equipment manufacturers, said Chauncey McIntosh, general manager of the F-35 Lightning II program. Smaller suppliers often lack dedicated repair lines and use the same equipment and workers for repair work that they use to manufacture new parts, which McIntosh said is inefficient. The agreement does not constitute a sales order, but Lockheed counts it as a prearranged long-term contract. The deal requires US congressional approval. $78-BILLION DEAL The least expensive version of the jet costs $92 million, so the [USN:L4N4680VI TEXT:"10-year framework agreement"] would be worth at least $78.2 billion. The Marines' F-35B short takeoff and landing version of the jet costs $121 million and the Navy's F-35C costs $110 million. The contract's mix of jets is unknown, and prices are expected to rise with inflation and labor costs. Lockheed, a supplier of missile-defense systems such as Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3) and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors, joined RTX (RTX.N) and Northrop Grumman (NOC.N) in [USN:L4N4660W1 TEXT:"raising forecasts this week"] on strong demand for munitions, air-defense systems and military aircraft. Lockheed expects 2026 sales of about $80 billion to $82 billion, up from its prior forecast of $79.75 billion to $81.75 billion. The company also lifted its annual earnings-per-share forecast to range between $30.35 and $30.75 from its previous view of $29.95 to $30.65. The company's backlog rose 27% sequentially to a record $292 billion, boosted by a $52.5 billion multiyear award for PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors, stockpiles of which were heavily used by US and allied forces in the Iran war. Lockheed raised its 2026 free cash flow forecast to about $7.8 billion to $8 billion, from $7 billion to $7.2 billion earlier. Sales for the quarter ended on September 27 rose 11% to $20.71 billion, driven by 24% growth in its missiles unit on higher PAC-3 and THAAD production and a 13% increase in aeronautics revenue from F-35 and C-130 programs. Analysts estimated $20.51 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Chief Financial Officer Evan Scott told Reuters a fourth-quarter increase in capital spending would be driven primarily by investments to expand munitions production capacity. Third-quarter profit of $7.97 per share came in above analysts' estimate of $7.43 per share.

item.title: Polymarket, Kalshi expand political donations as firms face state, federal scrutiny
item.description: Prediction market operators Kalshi, Polymarket and their founders have given at least $5 million combined to Republican and Democratic political groups this election cycle, according to campaign finance records and a private remittance document seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Douglas Gillison
item.content:encoded:
Prediction market operators Kalshi, Polymarket and their founders have given at least $5 million combined to Republican and Democratic political groups this election cycle, according to campaign finance records and a private remittance document seen by Reuters. The spending includes a previously unreported $1 million donation Polymarket made to a Democratic nonprofit that does not disclose its donors, the remittance document shows. Though a fraction of the [USN:L1N4310KM TEXT:"money spent by similar industries such as crypto"] and [USN:L6N43Q0T7 TEXT:"sports betting"], the companies' $5 million outlay is a sharp increase on the 2024 cycle, marking their first significant foray into political giving.

The pair have so far slightly favored Republicans, who received $2.7 million, with Democrats taking the remainder. Just over a third of the total cash went to state-level groups backing candidates for governor, attorney general and state legislatures, according to an analysis by the Center for Political Accountability (CPA), a transparency nonprofit. The spending surge comes as both companies [USN:L6N45G0XO TEXT:"battle state efforts to regulate their wagers as gambling"], and as they face growing scrutiny from federal lawmakers worried that prediction markets are spawning insider trading and undermining national security. "We have an industry where we're kind of figuring out the regulations on the fly," said David Primo, a professor of political science at the University of Rochester in New York. "If you're not engaging with these politicians, other people are going to be writing these regulations, and that could be an existential threat to these companies," he said. In a statement, Kalshi's head of federal government relations, John Bivona, said that by Election Day the company's full disclosures would show that its donations were roughly evenly distributed across both parties. "Regulation that keeps prediction markets safe for consumers and allows them to grow in America isn't a partisan issue," he added. A Polymarket spokesperson did not address questions about the company's donations but said in an email: "We engage with all sides of the debate and welcome conversations with anyone who wants to learn more about our platform." POLYMARKET CEO COPLAN STARTS GIVING TO REPUBLICANS Prediction markets allow wagers on an array of events, including sports games, elections and government announcements. Kalshi and Polymarket rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in [USN:L1N3M00OE TEXT:"signaling that President Donald Trump"], a Republican, would win the election. Trump's administration has generally supported the industry, although a handful of congressional Republicans have raised concerns about election betting. Democrats, meanwhile, have introduced multiple bills aimed at restricting prediction wagers. Polymarket Chief Executive Shayne Coplan, who previously donated almost exclusively to Democrats, has broadened his giving this cycle. Campaign finance records show that he and Polymarket have directed roughly $1.3 million to Republican committees and candidates, while also supporting Democratic groups. According to the remittance document seen by Reuters, Blockratize Inc, which operates as Polymarket, this summer transferred $1 million to House Majority Forward, a nonprofit that works to elect Democrats. Companies frequently donate via such tax-exempt "dark-money" organizations, which are not required to disclose their donors. Polymarket and Coplan gave the roughly $1.3 million combined to the Republican National Committee, as well as a super political action committee, or PAC, supporting House Republicans, and V-PAC, a super PAC which supports Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. Representatives for House Majority Forward and the Republican fundraising vehicles either declined to comment or did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not identify any political contributions by Kalshi founders Luana Lopes Lara and Tarek Mansour in publicly available campaign finance records for previous cycles. As of early October, they had given at least $1 million, about 72% of which went to Republican causes and candidates, campaign finance records show. COMPANIES GIVE TO STATE GROUPS AMID LEGAL FIGHT State gaming authorities, attorneys general and Native American tribes have sued to block Kalshi, Polymarket and others from offering sports bets, arguing that such wagers are gambling and subject to stringent state oversight. The companies say their wagers [USN:L6N43T15B TEXT:"are financial instruments"] overseen by federal agencies. This cycle, the companies began donating to groups that back state-level candidates who could determine how that fight unfolds, with spending accelerating over the past 12 months and so far marginally favoring Democrats, the CPA data shows. Kalshi has so far given nearly $1.5 million to such groups, split roughly evenly across both parties. Polymarket has so far given nearly $250,000 to two Democratic groups and one Republican group, the data shows. Jeanne Hanna, vice president for research at CPA, said the slight tilt toward Democratic groups could reflect an expectation that the party is poised for greater success at the state level this election cycle. In addition to funding campaigns, such state-level groups also allow companies to establish rapport with policymakers, she said. "There definitely is a membership structure in which larger contributions get you greater access," she added.

item.title: Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal
item.description: The possible merger may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between President Donald Trump and the Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Cassell Bryan-Low, Hyunjoo Jin
item.content:encoded: A possible merger between Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX (SPCX.O) and carmaker Tesla (TSLA.O) may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between US President Donald Trump and the Democrats. Musk revived speculation about [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"a tie-up"] this week, calling a combination "a good idea" and confirming that committees at both companies were reviewing a potential deal, a step toward what could become the largest merger in history and create a company worth about $3.5 trillion. But a merger would also unite one of the US government's most important aerospace and defense contractors with one of the most China-exposed major American manufacturers — a combination likely to raise questions about national security risks both in Washington and in Beijing. Those concerns are unlikely to derail a deal, analysts said, but they would likely leave the combined company exposed to years of political wrangling and pressure from both sides of the Pacific. Tesla's China operations, they said, could become a source of leverage for Beijing in any future dispute with Washington, while a Democratic takeover of the US House of Representatives in next month's midterm elections could subject the deal to congressional investigations and political maneuvering. Democrats immediately raised concerns about the deal's implications, signaling their intent to turn the merger into a political flashpoint ahead of the November 3 midterms. “If Elon Musk moves forward with the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, the deal would carry real risks that antitrust enforcers across the world would scrutinize," said US Senator Cory Booker, a New Jersey Democrat who sits on both the Judiciary and Foreign Relations committees. He added that he was prepared to conduct oversight of any deal: "When one person controls the infrastructure that governments and militaries depend on, his business decisions become national security decisions, too." Musk could seek to address concerns by limiting how closely the two companies are integrated. The greater threat to the deal may come later, however, if a future administration takes a harder line on the relationship between Tesla and a company increasingly tied to US national security, analysts said. "A merger agreement would involve pledges of limits to the connections between SpaceX and Tesla," said Derek Scissors, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute. "I don't think the Trump administration would enforce these limits. However, the next administration could certainly begin to scrutinize a merged entity. This may be the biggest risk to a deal - that it could get unwound in 2029." EXPOSURE TO CHINA For Beijing, a merger would effectively place Tesla's sprawling Shanghai manufacturing hub under the same corporate umbrella as SpaceX, a company that has become deeply embedded in US military and national security activities through its Pentagon work and through Starlink's role in conflicts, including Ukraine. "A formal merger would make it harder for Chinese authorities to treat Tesla as a purely commercial actor, raising risks for future factory expansions, data approvals, or market access," said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, a senior research fellow at the Brussels-based Bruegel think tank. Tesla's reliance on production from Shanghai already gives China considerable leverage over Musk's business empire. A merger could extend that control to a broader corporate group encompassing strategically important assets such as satellite communications, launch services and military-related technologies. GLOBAL REGULATORY HURDLES The deal would also have to navigate a maze of reviews around the world as competition authorities assess its impact on industries ranging from automobiles and satellite communications to artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Musk's close relationship with Trump would likely dispel concerns about potential US regulatory roadblocks to a transaction, analysts said, while antitrust experts see limited competition concerns because the companies operate largely in separate markets. Outside the United States, however, foreign regulators are likely to scrutinize whether a combined company would gain an unfair advantage by integrating technologies spanning automobiles, artificial intelligence and aerospace. Antitrust experts said authorities in markets with powerful domestic auto industries, such as China and South Korea, could examine whether Tesla's access to SpaceX technologies would give it an advantage that rivals cannot replicate, creating barriers for competitors and potentially undermining domestic manufacturers. Regulators could respond by requiring the company to license key technologies to competitors as part of any approval, said Ioannis Kokkoris, a law professor at Queen Mary University of London. A South Korean antitrust official told Reuters that the merger, if pursued, could require an in-depth review of its potential impact on that country's industries. "Korean antitrust officials will be wary of the merger. They will take the merger very seriously," said Lee Hwang, a law professor at Korea University and former Korea Fair Trade Commission official. "The stakes are very high in Korea because it regards both the automotive and aerospace sectors as strategically important industries."

item.title: Manchester City take perfect record to Villa amid off-field turmoil
item.description: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their guilty verdict on financial-rule charges.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"guilty verdict"] on financial-rule charges. Enzo Maresca's City have won all seven league matches to sit three points clear of champions Arsenal, but an independent commission's finding that the club were guilty of 114 financial breaches has cast a shadow over their blistering start.
